definition_zh: 本能；天性；与生俱来的行为倾向；内心的直觉冲动
definition_en: an inborn pattern of behaviour, or an inner impulse that drives action without conscious reasoning or learning
core_image: 一只刚破壳的幼鸟从未见过海，却径直朝海的方向走去，体内像有一根看不见的线在牵引
scene: 研究者把刚孵化的幼龟放在远离海面的沙地上，四周没有任何光亮提示，它们却一致朝海的方向爬去。 Hatchlings placed on sand far from the water still move toward the sea, as if guided by an instinct.
sceneCN: 这里 instinct 指「不经学习而与生俱来的行为倾向」（第 1 个义项：天生的行为驱动力）；句意为放在远离海面的沙地上的幼龟仍一致朝大海爬去，仿佛被本能引导。可辨识物件：沙地、幼龟、海平线、记录板。

pos.zh: 本能；与生俱来的行为倾向
直觉；内心的冲动（不作理性推理）
充满……的；由……驱动的（书面语，多与表示对象的介词连用）

forms.label: 形容词（本能的，心理学术语）

senses.title: An inborn pattern of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 与生俱来、不经学习的行为模式
senses.definition: a way of acting that an animal or person is born with and does not have to learn
senses.definitionCN: 动物或人与生俱来、无须学习就会采取的行为方式
senses.example: Migration is an instinct that no bird teaches its young.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙是一种没有哪只鸟会教给幼鸟的本能。
senses.why: The Latin noun instinctus first meant an inner prompting, so the word begins as something pushing from inside rather than something taught from outside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 instinctus 最初指内在的推动，因此这个词从一开始就是由内向外推的力量，而非外部教给的东西。

senses.title: An inner impulse driving action
senses.definition: a strong inner urge that makes someone act before thinking it through
senses.definitionCN: 使人来不及细想就行动的强烈内在冲动
senses.example: She pulled the child back from the kerb on instinct alone.
senses.exampleCN: 她单凭本能就把孩子从路缘拉回。
senses.why: The same prompting that guides a whole species also operates in a single moment, when the body moves before the mind has finished judging.
senses.whyCN: 引导整个物种的那种推动，也作用于某一瞬间：身体先动，理智还没判断完。

senses.title: A natural feel for something
senses.titleCN: 对某事天生的敏感与手感
senses.definition: a natural ability to notice or do something well without formal training
senses.definitionCN: 未经正式训练就能察觉或做好某事的天生能力
senses.example: A good editor has an instinct for the sentence that will confuse readers.
senses.exampleCN: 好编辑对会令读者困惑的句子有一种天生敏感。
senses.why: If an impulse can guide action, it can also guide attention, and attention sharpened into skill becomes what English calls an instinct for a craft.
senses.whyCN: 冲动既能引导行动，也能引导注意；当注意凝练成技艺，英语就说一个人对某行当有 instinct。

senses.title: The intuitive faculty as a whole
senses.definition: the general human capacity to reach a judgement without explicit reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 人不作明确推理就能作出判断的整体能力
senses.example: Detectives learn to balance evidence against instinct.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探要学会在证据与直觉之间取得平衡。
senses.why: Once the singular prompting was generalized, instinct came to name a whole faculty, the counterpart of step-by-step reason.
senses.whyCN: 当单次的推动被一般化，instinct 就开始指一整套能力，成为逐步推理的对照面。

senses.title: An unlearned response in ethology
senses.titleCN: 动物行为学中的非学习反应
senses.definition: in ethology, a stereotyped response that appears without learning and is triggered by a specific sign
senses.definitionCN: 在动物行为学中，由特定信号触发、不经学习便出现的刻板反应
senses.example: The chick's gaping response to a red spot is treated as an instinct.
senses.exampleCN: 雏鸟见到红点就张口这一反应被当作一种本能。
senses.why: Twentieth-century ethologists needed a word for behaviour that survives isolation from other animals, and they took the oldest sense of the noun and tightened it into a technical one.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的行为学家需要一个词来指即使隔离饲养也照样出现的行为，于是把名词最古老的义项收窄为术语。

senses.title: A sudden prompting or urge
senses.titleCN: 突如其来的冲动或念头
senses.definition: a brief, powerful impulse to say or do something at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某一刻突然涌起、想说话或想做事的强烈短促冲动
senses.example: His first instinct was to deny everything.
senses.exampleCN: 他的第一个念头是把一切否认掉。
senses.why: The earliest English sense was exactly this: a prompting, something put into the mind. The modern 'first instinct' phrasing keeps that shape intact.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的意思正是这个：一种被放进心里的推动。现代说法「第一个念头」保留了这一形态。

senses.title: The instinctive part of character
senses.titleCN: 性格中属于本能的成分
senses.definition: the layer of a person's character that is felt as innate rather than cultivated
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格中被感受为天生而非后天养成的层面
senses.example: Years of training never quite silenced the instinct in him.
senses.exampleCN: 多年训练始终没能完全压住他身上的那股本能。
senses.why: If instinct is what is born with us, it can be spoken of as a possession, a part of the self that training only covers over.
senses.whyCN: 既然本能是与生俱来的，就可以被当作一种所有物来说，是训练只能覆盖、不能取消的那部分自我。

senses.title: Instinct as the opposite of reason
senses.titleCN: 哲学中与理性相对的本能
senses.definition: in philosophy and psychology, the non-rational source of action set against deliberate reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学与心理学中，与审慎推理相对的非理性行动来源
senses.example: The essay sets instinct against calculation and asks which one actually governs markets.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把本能与算计对立起来，追问究竟哪一个在支配市场。
senses.why: Once instinct named a faculty, thinkers could place it on one side of a great divide, opposite the calculating mind, and argue about which side really rules.
senses.whyCN: 当 instinct 成为一种能力的名称，思想家就能把它放在一道大分界的一侧，与算计的心智相对，并争论哪一侧真正主宰。

intro.en: Instinct comes through Old French from Latin instinctus 'an instigation, impulse', a noun made from the past participle of instinguere 'to incite, goad'. The deeper root is the prick or point that also lies behind stick.
intro.cn: instinct 经古法语来自拉丁 instinctus「煽动、冲动」，该名词由 instinguere「刺激、驱赶」的过去分词构成。更深的词根是「刺、尖」，也与 stick 背后的词根同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning 'to prick, stick, pierce', reconstructed from forms in Latin, Greek and Indo-Iranian; it is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 一个重构的印欧词根，意为「刺、扎、穿」，由拉丁语、希腊语与印度-伊朗语族的形式重构而来；它是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Stinguere meant 'to prick, goad'. It is a different verb from the stinguere behind extinguish 'to quench', although the two forms look identical in dictionaries.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、驱赶」。它与构成 extinguish「熄灭」的那个 stinguere 并不是同一个动词，尽管两者在词典里写法相同。

items.en: In- 'into, on' plus stinguere produced instinguere 'to incite, impel', whose past participle instinctus gave the noun meaning 'a prompting, an inspiration'.
items.cn: in-「进入、向」加 stinguere 构成 instinguere「煽动、推动」，其过去分词 instinctus 给出名词义「推动、灵感」。

items.en: Old French instinct entered English in the early fifteenth century as 'a prompting'. The sense 'animal faculty of intuitive perception' follows from the mid-fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 instinct 在 15 世纪初进入英语，义为「推动」。到 15 世纪中叶起，出现「动物凭直觉感知的能力」这一义项。

items.en: The broad sense 'natural tendency' is recorded from the 1560s, and the technical behavioural sense belongs to nineteenth- and twentieth-century science.
items.cn: 泛化的「天然倾向」义自 16 世纪 60 年代有记录，行为学的术语义则属于 19 至 20 世纪的科学语境。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): etymologists have tried to link *steig- with the root of sting, but the attempt is described as having formal problems, so any single Indo-European parent for both families is a reconstruction, not a settled fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：词源学家曾试图把 *steig- 与 sting 的词根联系起来，但这一尝试被认为存在形式上的问题，因此为这两个词族设定单一印欧语母体只是重构，并非定论。

note.en: The first group separates words that look like instinct but come from other roots; the second group holds near neighbours that name the same inner pressure from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似与 instinct 同源、其实来自别的词根的词；第二组是语义相近、从不同角度指同一种内在压力的词。

entries.definition: The adjective built on instinct with -ive; it describes a reaction, while instinct names the drive itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 instinct 加 -ive 构成的形容词，描述一种反应，而 instinct 指驱动力本身。

entries.definition: A later doublet meaning the same as instinctive but favoured in psychoanalytic writing.
entries.definitionCN: 后出的同义词，与 instinctive 同义，但更受精神分析写作偏爱。

entries.definition: From Latin intueri 'to look at', built on tueri 'to watch': knowledge by direct looking, not by an inborn drive.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 intueri「观看」，由 tueri「注视」构成：靠直接观看得到的知识，而非天生驱动力。

entries.definition: From ex- plus the homographic stinguere 'to quench', a different Latin verb from the stinguere 'to prick' behind instinct.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ex- 加同形的 stinguere「熄灭」，与构成 instinct 的 stinguere「刺」并非同一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A sudden urge to act, from Latin pellere 'to drive'; it stresses the moment, while instinct stresses the inborn source.
entries.definitionCN: 突然想行动的冲动，来自拉丁 pellere「推动」；它强调瞬间，instinct 强调天生来源。

entries.definition: A persistent internal force that motivates behaviour, often used in psychology for hunger, thirst or sex.
entries.definitionCN: 持续驱动行为的内在力量，心理学中常用于饥饿、口渴或性。

entries.definition: A natural ability to learn or do something, from Latin aptus 'fitted'; it points to capacity rather than to a prompting.
entries.definitionCN: 学习或做好某事的天生能力，来自拉丁 aptus「合适的」；它指能力倾向，而非内在推动。

entries.definition: An automatic bodily response to a stimulus, mediated by the nervous system; narrower and more mechanical than instinct.
entries.definitionCN: 身体对刺激的自动反应，由神经系统传导；比 instinct 更窄、更机械。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' + stinguere 'prick': something pricked into you from birth.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ stinguere「刺」：从出生起就被刺进你体内的东西。

normal.en: The family runs instinct, instinctive, instinctively, instinctual, instinctiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 instinct、instinctive、instinctively、instinctual、instinctiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sense: by instinct, survival instinct, maternal instinct.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出词义：出于本能、求生本能、母性本能。

normal.en: Extinguish looks like a relative but uses a different Latin verb meaning 'to quench'.
normal.cn: extinguish 看似同族，其实用的是另一个意为「熄灭」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Ethology uses the noun for behaviour present without learning, as in the chick's gaping response.
normal.cn: 行为学用这个名词指不经学习就出现的行为，如雏鸟的张嘴反应。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that already knows which way is up before it has seen the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子在见到太阳之前就已经知道哪边是上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling back from the stove before the mind has named the heat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在头脑还没说出「烫」之前就已缩回。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle that never asks for instructions and still points north.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从不请求指示、却始终指向北方的罗盘针。

examples.en: Birds navigate by instinct rather than by anything they are taught.
examples.cn: 鸟类靠本能而非任何被教给的本领导航。

examples.en: Her first instinct was to call for help.
examples.cn: 她的第一个反应是呼救。

examples.en: The essay contrasts instinct with deliberate calculation.
examples.cn: 这篇文章把本能与审慎算计作了对照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印（in）+ 死盯（stinct）」——小动物一出生就死死盯住某个方向，好像天生被印进去一样 → 本能

root: 拉丁 instinctus「推动、冲动」= in-（向内）+ stinguere「刺、驱赶」（其更早来源为重构的 *steig-）；与 extinguish 所用「熄灭」义的 stinguere 不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a force planted inside an animal, which acts without teaching, then narrows into a moment's urge, widens into a whole faculty, and finally stands opposite reason itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：一股被植入动物体内的力量，不经教导就能行动；它先收窄为某一瞬的冲动，再扩为整体能力，最后站到理性的对立面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner thread pulling a newborn creature in a direction it has never been shown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根内在的线，把新生的小生命拉向从未有人给它指过的方向。

branches.en: BORN-WITH BEHAVIOUR: whether described in plain words or as an ethological category, nothing here had to be learned.
branches.cn: 与生俱来的行为：无论用日常说法还是行为学术语，这里没有一样是学来的。

branches.en: INNER PUSH: the same force seen as a lasting drive and as a single sharp moment.
branches.cn: 内在推动：同一股力量，既表现为持久驱力，也表现为一次尖锐的瞬间。

branches.en: FROM URGE TO FACULTY: repeated prompting hardens into a feel for a craft, then into intuition as a whole.
branches.cn: 从冲动到能力：反复的推动凝成对某行当的手感，再扩为整体的直觉。

branches.en: PART OF THE SELF: what is inborn can be spoken of as a possession that training only covers.
branches.cn: 自我的一部分：天生之物可以当作一种所有物来说，训练只能覆盖它。

branches.en: THE GREAT DIVIDE: once named as a faculty, instinct is placed against calculation and argued over.
branches.cn: 大分界：一旦被命名为一种能力，本能就被放到算计的对面，成为争论对象。

intro.en: Instinct is a Latin verb form with two recognisable pieces, and both pieces also build ordinary English words, so the spelling rewards a morpheme-by-morpheme reading.
intro.cn: instinct 是一个拉丁动词形式，含两个可辨识的成分；这两个成分还构成常见的英语词，因此按语素读这个拼写是有回报的。

latinIntro.en: Latin instinguere and its participle instinctus give the English noun; the prefix in- and the root stinguere recur in other words, though not all look-alikes share this root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 instinguere 及其分词 instinctus 给出这个英语名词；前缀 in- 与词根 stinguere 在别的词中重现，但并非所有形近词都共用这个词根。

items.example: The prefix turns a prick into something driven into the mind.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「刺」变成「刺进心里」的东西。

items.example: The root supplies the sharpness of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供意象中的尖锐感。

items.example: Migration is guided by instinct.
items.exampleCN: 迁徙由本能引导。

items.example: She gave an instinctive answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给出了一个本能的回答。

items.example: He instinctively ducked.
items.exampleCN: 他本能地低下头。

items.example: Psychologists speak of instinctual drives.
items.exampleCN: 心理学家谈本能的驱力。

items.example: The study measured the instinctiveness of the response.
items.exampleCN: 该研究测量了这一反应的本能性。

items.example: The character is written as almost instinctless, all calculation.
items.exampleCN: 这个人物被写成几乎没有本能、全靠算计。

definition_zh: 本能的；直觉的；不假思索的；与生俱来的
definition_en: based on or produced by instinct rather than by reasoning, learning or deliberate choice
core_image: 手离滚烫的锅还有一寸时已经缩回，动作比意识更早一步
scene: 孩子第一次看见盘起来的绳子就立刻缩手后退，还没来得及判断那到底是什么。 The child withdrew from the coiled rope before any reasoned check, an instinctive response to a shape that resembles a threat.
sceneCN: 这里 instinctive 指「由本能驱动、不经理性判断的反应」（第 1 个义项：源自本能而非推理的反应）；句意为孩子还没来得及辨认就缩手后退，那是对形似威胁之物的一种本能反应。可辨识物件：盘起的绳子、缩回的手、孩子的侧脸。

forms.label: 同义形容词（心理学常用）

senses.title: Produced by instinct, not reasoning
senses.titleCN: 由本能而非推理产生的
senses.definition: coming from an inborn drive rather than from conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 源自天生的驱力，而非有意识的思考
senses.example: Her instinctive grip on the rail saved her from the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 她本能地抓住栏杆，才没有摔下去。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the noun into a description of what a reaction comes from, so instinctive marks the source of the act: instinct, not judgement.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把名词转为描述反应来源的形容词，因此 instinctive 标出动作的来源：是本能，不是判断。

senses.title: Done without deliberation
senses.definition: happening so quickly that no deliberate weighing of options takes place
senses.definitionCN: 发生得太快，根本没有对选项作有意的权衡
senses.example: He gave an instinctive nod before he had heard the whole offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没听完整个提议就本能地点了头。
senses.why: What comes from instinct arrives before deliberation can finish; the adjective therefore also describes the speed of the act.
senses.whyCN: 出于本能的东西在斟酌完成前就到了，因此这个形容词也描述动作的速度。

senses.title: Innate rather than acquired
senses.definition: present from birth rather than built up by training or experience
senses.definitionCN: 自出生起就有，而非经训练或经验积累形成
senses.example: The paper asks whether rhythm is instinctive or learned.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文追问节奏感是天生的还是学来的。
senses.why: Instinct names what an animal has without learning, so the adjective naturally marks the boundary between nature and training.
senses.whyCN: instinct 指动物不经学习就有的东西，因此这个形容词自然用来划出天性与训练的界线。

senses.title: Unlearned behaviour in ethology
senses.titleCN: 行为学意义上的非学习行为
senses.definition: in ethology, describing a fixed response elicited by a sign stimulus without prior experience
senses.definitionCN: 在行为学中，描述由信号刺激引发、无需先前经验的固定反应
senses.example: The team recorded an instinctive pecking sequence in chicks raised alone.
senses.exampleCN: 研究组记录了单独饲养的雏鸟身上那套本能的啄食序列。
senses.why: Ethologists adopted the adjective for behaviour that isolation cannot erase, giving the everyday word a controlled technical use.
senses.whyCN: 行为学家用这个形容词指隔离也抹不掉的行为，使日常词获得受控的术语用法。

senses.title: Automatic in style
senses.definition: describing a movement or judgement so practised that it feels automatic
senses.definitionCN: 形容动作或判断熟练到近乎自动
senses.example: Years of practice had made his footwork instinctive.
senses.exampleCN: 多年练习使他的步法近乎自动。
senses.why: Training can make a learned skill feel unlearned; the adjective then borrows the sense of 'effortless' from its core meaning.
senses.whyCN: 训练能让学来的技艺感觉像没学过；这个形容词于是从核心义借来「不费力」的意思。

senses.title: Deeply rooted in character
senses.definition: describing a tendency that seems part of a person's basic nature
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种倾向仿佛是某人基本天性的一部分
senses.example: His instinctive distrust of slogans never left him.
senses.exampleCN: 他对口号那种本能的不信任从未离开过他。
senses.why: If instinct can be treated as a part of the self, the adjective can describe traits that feel inseparable from who someone is.
senses.whyCN: 既然本能可被当作自我的一部分，这个形容词就能描述那些仿佛与某人不可分割的特质。

senses.title: Immediate and unreasoned in judgement
senses.titleCN: 判断上即时且未经理性的
senses.definition: of a judgement, reached at once and without explicit evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容判断当即作出、没有明示证据
senses.example: Reviewers often reach an instinctive verdict in the first ten seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 评审者常在最初十秒就作出本能的判断。
senses.why: The word can describe verdicts as well as movements: what is instant and unreasoned looks the same whether it is a hand or an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能形容动作也能形容判断：无论缩手还是形成意见，即时而不经理性的样子是一样的。

senses.title: Abstract: belonging to the nature of a thing
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：属于事物本性的
senses.definition: used of a quality that appears to belong to the very nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某种仿佛属于事物本性的特质
senses.example: The novelist treats loyalty as instinctive in dogs and negotiable in people.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家把忠诚写成狗的本性，而在人身上则可有可无。
senses.why: At its widest, the adjective no longer needs a creature: any quality said to be built into a thing's nature can be called instinctive.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个形容词不再需要生命体：任何被称为「天生嵌在事物本性里」的特质都可叫 instinctive。

intro.en: Instinctive is an English adjective formed on the Latin participle stem instinct- plus the suffix -ive. It appears in the 1640s, and its adverb instinctively follows within a few decades.
intro.cn: instinctive 是英语形容词，由拉丁分词词干 instinct- 加后缀 -ive 构成，17 世纪 40 年代出现，其副词 instinctively 在数十年内随之出现。

items.en: The stem comes from instinctus, the past participle of instinguere 'to incite, goad', so the adjective inherits the image of something driven in.
items.cn: 该词干来自 instinctus，即 instinguere「煽动、驱赶」的过去分词，因此这个形容词继承了「被推入」的意象。

items.en: Latin -ivus formed adjectives of tendency or function; English -ive does the same, as in active, decisive and instinctive.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ivus 构成表示倾向或功能的形容词；英语 -ive 作用相同，如 active、decisive、instinctive。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the 1640s, built directly on the noun rather than borrowed whole from a Latin adjective.
items.cn: 该形容词自 17 世纪 40 年代有记录，直接由名词构成，而非整体借自某个拉丁形容词。

items.en: Instinctively is recorded from the 1610s in the sources, and instinctiveness follows; the family kept growing by ordinary English suffixation.
items.cn: 据所查资料，instinctively 自 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，instinctiveness 随之出现；这个词族靠普通英语后缀不断扩展。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century biology gave the adjective a technical role in descriptions of unlearned behaviour.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的生物学赋予这个形容词描述非学习行为的技术角色。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries differ on whether the earliest citation for instinctively belongs to the 1610s or later, and the pre-Latin origin of stinguere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各词典对 instinctively 最早书证属于 17 世纪 10 年代还是更晚并不一致；stinguere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one distinguishes adjectives that look related but are built on other stems; group two holds near synonyms that differ in whether they stress origin, speed or feeling.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似相关、其实由别的词干构成的形容词；第二组是近义词，区别在于强调来源、速度还是感受。

entries.definition: A later variant built with -ual instead of -ive; psychology prefers it, but the meaning is essentially the same.
entries.definitionCN: 后出的变体，用 -ual 而非 -ive 构成；心理学更偏爱它，但意思基本相同。

entries.definition: From Latin intueri 'to look at'; it describes knowing by direct perception, with no inborn drive implied.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 intueri「观看」；描述靠直接感知而知晓，不含天生驱力之意。

entries.definition: From distinguere 'to separate', not stinguere 'to prick': it means marking something off as different.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 distinguere「区分」，而非 stinguere「刺」：意为把某物标出、使之有别。

entries.definition: Built on the 'quench' verb behind extinguish; it means tending to put out or wipe out, not inborn.
entries.definitionCN: 由构成 extinguish 的「熄灭」动词构成；意为倾向于熄灭或消灭，与天生无关。

entries.definition: Working by itself without conscious control; it stresses mechanism, while instinctive stresses biological origin.
entries.definitionCN: 无需意识控制自行运作；强调机制，instinctive 强调生物来源。

entries.definition: Happening without the will's consent, as a sneeze; it says nothing about whether the source is inborn.
entries.definitionCN: 未经意志同意就发生，如打喷嚏；不涉及来源是否天生。

entries.definition: Present from birth, from Latin innatus; it describes the possession, not the reaction that flows from it.
entries.definitionCN: 自出生就有，来自拉丁 innatus；描述所拥有的特质，而非由之产生的反应。

entries.definition: Informal for a predictably automatic reaction; it carries criticism that instinctive does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对可预料自动反应的口语说法；带有 instinctive 所没有的贬义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: instinct + -ive: the adjective simply says 'coming from instinct'.
normal.cn: instinct + -ive：这个形容词只是说「来自本能」。

normal.en: The family runs instinct, instinctive, instinctively, instinctual, instinctiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 instinct、instinctive、instinctively、instinctual、instinctiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: instinctive reaction, instinctive fear, instinctive avoidance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：本能反应、本能的恐惧、本能的回避。

normal.en: Intuitive looks similar but comes from intueri 'to look', not from stinguere.
normal.cn: intuitive 看似相近，其实来自 intueri「观看」，并非 stinguere。

normal.en: The adverb instinctively usually sits next to the verb: instinctively ducked, instinctively knew.
normal.cn: 副词 instinctively 通常紧挨动词：本能地低头、本能地知道。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that retreats a heartbeat before the brain files its report.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在头脑递交报告前的一瞬就已收回。

abstract.en: Picture a door that locks itself the instant it senses heat.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门一感到热度就自己上锁。

abstract.en: Picture a musician whose fingers find the chord while the mind is still reading the score.
abstract.cn: 想象乐手的手指在头脑还在读谱时就已找到和弦。

examples.en: Pulling her hand from the flame was instinctive.
examples.cn: 把手从火焰上抽回是本能的。

examples.en: He has an instinctive sense of where the story should end.
examples.cn: 他对故事该在哪里结束有一种本能的判断。

examples.en: The chicks showed an instinctive response to the shadow overhead.
examples.cn: 雏鸟对头顶的阴影表现出本能反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「instinct（本能）+ ive（……的）」——像被本能推着走一样的 → 本能的、不假思索的

root: instinct（拉丁 instinctus「推动」）+ -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表倾向）；核心为「由内生推动而来」，与 intuitive（intueri 观看）不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one claim: the act did not come from reasoning. They then vary the setting, from reflexes and ethology to trained skill, character and abstract nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个判断展开：这个动作不来自推理。随后变换场景，从反射与行为学，到训练出的技艺、性格与抽象本性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a movement that begins before the mind has finished its check.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个在头脑完成核对之前就已开始的行动。

branches.en: SOURCE AND SPEED: the act is traced to instinct, and that origin is what makes it instant.
branches.cn: 来源与速度：动作被追溯到本能，而正是这个来源使它即时。

branches.en: NATURE VERSUS TRAINING: the everyday claim becomes a controlled ethological category.
branches.cn: 天性与训练：日常判断变成受控的行为学范畴。

branches.en: TRAINED TO FEEL UNTRAINED: practice can make a learned movement borrow the look of instinct.
branches.cn: 练到像没练：练习能让学来的动作借来本能的外表。

branches.en: CHARACTER AND VERDICT: the same adjective covers lasting traits and snap judgements.
branches.cn: 性格与判断：同一个形容词既覆盖持久特质，也覆盖瞬间判断。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any quality felt to belong to a thing's nature.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何被感受为属于事物本性的特质。

intro.en: Instinctive is a transparent derivative: a Latin noun stem plus a Latin adjective suffix, both of which recur across English.
intro.cn: instinctive 是一个透明的派生词：拉丁名词词干加拉丁形容词后缀，两者在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The stem instinct- goes back to Latin instinctus; -ive goes back to -ivus, the suffix of tendency seen in active and decisive.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 instinct- 可追溯到拉丁 instinctus；-ive 可追溯到 -ivus，即见于 active 与 decisive 的倾向后缀。

items.example: The stem names the source of the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干点出反应的来源。

items.example: Active, decisive and instinctive share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: active、decisive 与 instinctive 共用这个后缀。

items.example: The recoil was instinctive.
items.exampleCN: 这一退缩是本能的。

items.example: She instinctively stepped back.
items.exampleCN: 她本能地退后一步。

items.example: Judges rated the instinctiveness of each reply.
items.exampleCN: 评审者给每个回答的本能性打了分。

items.example: Instinctual fear precedes language.
items.exampleCN: 本能的恐惧先于语言出现。

items.example: The study separates learned from non-instinctive responses.
items.exampleCN: 该研究把习得反应与非本能反应分开。

items.example: Critics called the performance technically perfect but uninstinctive.
items.exampleCN: 评论者说这场表演技术上完美，却缺乏本能。

definition_zh: 行为；举止；表现方式；（心理学）可观察到的反应
definition_en: the way a person, animal or thing acts, especially as observed by others
core_image: 同一个人在婚礼上和在球场上判若两人：同一副身体，在不同场合摆出两套完全不同的动作
scene: 观察站里，研究员不记录动物发出什么声音，只记录它们何时进食、何时理毛、何时退到角落。 The observers ignore every sound and record only when the animal feeds, grooms or retreats, treating behavior as whatever can be seen.
sceneCN: 这里 behavior 指「可被观察到的动作与反应的总和」（第 1 个义项：外在行为举止）；句意为研究者不看叫声，只记录进食、理毛、退避等可见动作。可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、正在理毛的动物、墙角的阴影。

pos.zh: （心理学）可观察的反应；行为表现
（系统、材料等的）运行表现；反应方式

senses.title: Observable conduct
senses.titleCN: 可被观察到的行为举止
senses.definition: the actions and reactions of a person or animal that others can see
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物做出的、他人可见的动作与反应
senses.example: The zookeepers logged the feeding behavior of each group.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员记录了每一组的进食行为。
senses.why: The word grew out of behave, which meant to hold or carry oneself in a certain way, so behavior begins as the outward shape of that carrying.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 behave 发展而来，原义是「以某种方式把握自己」，因此 behavior 最初就是这种自我把握的外在形状。

senses.title: Manner of acting in a situation
senses.titleCN: 在特定场合的应对方式
senses.definition: the way someone acts in a particular situation or under particular conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某人在特定情境或条件下行动的方式
senses.example: His behavior under pressure surprised the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 他在压力下的表现让全队吃惊。
senses.why: Since conduct always happens somewhere, the word naturally attaches to a setting and describes how someone handles it.
senses.whyCN: 举止总发生在某个场合，因此这个词自然附着于情境，描述某人如何应对。

senses.title: Social conduct and manners
senses.titleCN: 社交场合的举止与礼貌
senses.definition: the degree to which someone acts politely or acceptably in company
senses.definitionCN: 某人在人前表现得有礼、得体的程度
senses.example: The children were told to be on their best behavior.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被叮嘱要表现得格外规矩。
senses.why: In company, the same outward conduct is judged by others, so behavior acquired a moral tinge: good behavior, bad behavior.
senses.whyCN: 在人前，同样的外在举止会被他人评判，于是 behavior 带上道德色彩：好行为、坏行为。

senses.title: Observable response in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的可观察反应
senses.definition: in psychology, any response that can be recorded from outside rather than inferred from inner states
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，可从外部记录、而非由内在状态推断的反应
senses.example: Behaviorists study behavior because it can be counted.
senses.exampleCN: 行为主义者研究行为，因为行为可以被计数。
senses.why: A school of psychology deliberately narrowed the word to what is visible, so that claims could be tested without guessing at feelings.
senses.whyCN: 一个心理学流派有意把词义收窄到可见之物，这样提出论断时无需猜测感受。

senses.title: Animal behavior as a subject
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的动物行为
senses.definition: the whole range of actions of an animal species, considered as a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种的全部动作，作为一个研究领域来看待
senses.example: The course covers the behavior of primates in the wild.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授野生灵长类的行为。
senses.why: Once conduct is an observable object, it can be collected, compared and named as a subject, which is what a science of behavior does.
senses.whyCN: 一旦举止成为可观察的客体，就能被收集、比较并命名为一门科目，这正是行为科学做的事。

senses.title: How a system or machine behaves
senses.titleCN: 系统或机器的运行表现
senses.definition: the way a machine, program or system acts when it operates
senses.definitionCN: 机器、程序或系统运转时的表现方式
senses.example: Engineers tested the behavior of the valve at low pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试了阀门在低压下的表现。
senses.why: English readily transfers human conduct to any working thing; a valve that sticks is said to behave badly, and its conduct is its behavior.
senses.whyCN: 英语很自然地把人的举止转移到任何运作之物上：卡住的阀门被说成「表现不好」，其表现就是 behavior。

senses.title: Response of a material or substance
senses.titleCN: 材料或物质在条件下的反应
senses.definition: the response of a material to heat, force, light or another condition
senses.definitionCN: 材料对热、力、光或其他条件的反应
senses.example: The team mapped the behavior of the alloy at high temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 研究组测明了该合金在高温下的表现。
senses.why: The transfer goes further still: what a substance does under a condition can be observed and recorded exactly as an animal's actions can.
senses.whyCN: 这种转移更进一步：物质在某种条件下的反应，完全可以像动物动作一样被观察和记录。

senses.title: Abstract: the way anything conducts itself
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何事物的行事方式
senses.definition: the characteristic way something acts or carries itself, including abstract things
senses.definitionCN: 某物行动或表现出的典型方式，包括抽象事物
senses.example: The behavior of prices in a panic follows no simple rule.
senses.exampleCN: 恐慌中价格的表现并不遵循简单规则。
senses.why: At its widest the word needs no body at all: anything that can be said to conduct itself can have a behavior.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词完全不需要身体：凡可说成「有其行事方式」的东西，都可以有 behavior。

intro.en: Behavior is an English noun built on behave, itself be- plus have in the sense 'to carry oneself'. Its ending came not from a Latin suffix but from the Middle English noun havour 'possession', remade under the influence of have.
intro.cn: behavior 是建立在 behave 之上的英语名词，而 behave 由 be- 加 have（「把握自己」）构成。它的词尾并非来自拉丁后缀，而是来自中古英语名词 havour「拥有」，受 have 影响而改写。

items.en: Habban 'to own, possess, hold' comes from Proto-Germanic *habejanan and the reconstructed PIE root *kap- 'to grasp'.
items.cn: habban「拥有、持有」来自原始日耳曼语 *habejanan 与重构的印欧词根 *kap-「抓握」。

items.en: The English intensive prefix be- was added to have in the fifteenth century to make the reflexive verb behave, literally 'to carry oneself'.
items.cn: 15 世纪时，英语的强调前缀 be- 加到 have 上，构成反身动词 behave，字面即「把握自己」。

items.en: The noun havour 'possession, demeanour' came from Old French aveir 'to have', and was reshaped in English by the influence of have.
items.cn: 名词 havour「拥有、举止」来自古法语 aveir「拥有」，并在英语中受 have 影响而改形。

items.en: Behavior is recorded from the late fifteenth century meaning 'conduct, manner of conducting oneself'. The American spelling dropped the u of behaviour.
items.cn: behavior 自 15 世纪晚期有记录，义为「举止、为人行事的方式」。美式拼写去掉了 behaviour 中的 u。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century psychology made behavior a technical term for externally observable response, and the plural behaviors spread with that use.
items.cn: 自 19 世纪晚期起，心理学把 behavior 变成「外部可观察反应」的术语，复数 behaviors 随这一用法扩散。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact formation): etymologists agree on be- plus have but disagree on whether the modern sense grew from the Old English compound behabban 'to contain' or from the newer 'carry oneself' model, and no single first citation is settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切构成）：词源学家一致同意是 be- 加 have，但对现代义究竟出自古英语复合词 behabban「容纳」还是出自较新的「把握自己」模式并无定论，最早书证也不统一。

note.en: Group one separates the look-alike nouns and adjectives of the same English family; group two holds near synonyms that judge conduct from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一英语词族中形近的名词与形容词；第二组是近义词，从不同角度评价举止。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to act or carry oneself in a particular way, literally 'to have oneself'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：以某种方式行动或把握自己，字面为「拥有自己」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of or concerning behavior', common in psychology and management.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「行为方面的」的形容词，常见于心理学与管理学。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same word; no difference in meaning, only in orthography.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，意义无差别，只在正字法上不同。

entries.definition: From be- plus hæs 'command', a native word meaning an order; it is not built on have and not a relative of behavior.
entries.definitionCN: 由 be- 加 hæs「命令」构成的本族词，意为吩咐；并非建立在 have 上，与 behavior 无亲缘。

entries.definition: A formal noun for how someone behaves, often with moral or professional judgement; from Latin conducere 'to lead together'.
entries.definitionCN: 指人如何行事的正式名词，常带道德或职业评判；来自拉丁 conducere「引导到一起」。

entries.definition: The outward manner and bearing a person shows, especially calmness or friendliness; it is about impression, not actions.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人显露在外的举止与神态，尤其指沉稳或友善；讲的是给人的印象，而非具体动作。

entries.definition: The plural noun for socially correct ways of behaving, judged by politeness rather than by observation.
entries.definitionCN: 指社交上得体的行为方式，以礼貌而非可观察性来评判。

entries.definition: A single thing done; behavior is the pattern of many actions, while an action can be counted one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 单个做完的事；behavior 是众多动作形成的模式，而 action 可逐个计数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: be- 'thoroughly' + have 'hold oneself': behavior is how one holds oneself in view of others.
normal.cn: be-「彻底」+ have「把握自己」：behavior 就是在他人眼中如何把握自己。

normal.en: The family runs behave, behavior, behavioral, behaviorally, behaviorism, misbehavior.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 behave、behavior、behavioral、behaviorally、behaviorism、misbehavior。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: social behavior, behavior pattern, on one's best behavior.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：社会行为、行为模式、表现得格外规矩。

normal.en: Latin habere 'to have' looks like have but is not related; the Latin cognate is capere 'to seize'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 habere「拥有」看似与 have 同源，其实无关；真正的拉丁同族是 capere「抓取」。

normal.en: Behaviorism made the word countable: one behavior, two behaviors, recorded from outside.
normal.cn: 行为主义使这个词可数：一个行为、两个行为，都从外部记录。

abstract.en: Picture a person wearing two different sets of gestures in two different rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个人在两个房间里换了两套完全不同的手势。

abstract.en: Picture a valve that either opens smoothly or sticks, and call that its conduct.
abstract.cn: 想象一只阀门要么顺滑开启、要么卡住，然后把这种表现称作它的行为。

abstract.en: Picture a price curve that panics in the same shape as a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一条价格曲线，恐慌时的形状和人潮一模一样。

examples.en: The study compared the behavior of trained and untrained dogs.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了受过训练与未受训练狗的行为。

examples.en: Nothing in her behavior suggested that she was worried.
examples.cn: 她的举止中没有任何迹象表明她在担心。

examples.en: Engineers model the behavior of the bridge under heavy wind.
examples.cn: 工程师对这座桥在强风下的表现建立模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「be（是）+ have（拥有）」——你「是怎样」就「拥有怎样的举止」 → 行为、举止

root: 英语 behave（be- 强调 + have「把握自己」）+ 名词词尾 -ior（受中古英语 havour 影响）；本族日耳曼来源，与拉丁 habere 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: conduct is first what can be seen, then what is seen in a setting, then what is judged, then what is counted by science, and finally what any working thing does.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：举止先是可见之物，再是特定场合中的可见之物，再是被评判之物，再是被科学计数之物，最后是任何运作之物的表现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one body carrying itself differently in different rooms.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一副身体，在不同房间里以不同方式把握自己。

branches.en: SEEN AND JUDGED: the same outward conduct is first recorded, then graded as good or bad.
branches.cn: 被看见与被评判：同样的外在举止先被记录，再被评好坏。

branches.en: IN A SETTING: conduct always answers a situation, so the word names the answer.
branches.cn: 处于情境：举止总在回应某个场合，于是这个词命名那个回应。

branches.en: MADE AN OBJECT: psychology turns conduct into countable data, and a science takes it as a subject.
branches.cn: 成为客体：心理学把举止变成可计数的数据，一门科学再把它当作研究对象。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED TO THINGS: machines and materials are said to behave, so their responses become behavior.
branches.cn: 转移到物：机器与材料被说成「表现」，其反应也就成了 behavior。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: anything with a characteristic way of acting.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何有其典型行事方式的东西。

intro.en: Behavior is not a Latin derivative but a native verb with a borrowed-looking noun ending; reading its two living parts, be- and have, is more useful than guessing at a suffix.
intro.cn: behavior 不是拉丁派生词，而是本族动词加上一个看似借来的名词词尾；读出它两个活着的成分 be- 与 have，比猜测某个后缀更有用。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for the word itself: have is Germanic, and the Latin verb habere 'to have' is a false friend. The Latin cognate, at the level of the reconstructed root *kap-, is capere 'to seize'.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身没有拉丁来源：have 属日耳曼语，拉丁 habere「拥有」只是形似的假朋友。在重构词根 *kap- 的层面，真正的拉丁同族是 capere「抓取」。

items.example: The prefix makes the verb reflexive: to behave is to act upon oneself.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使动词带反身意味：behave 就是对自己施加动作。

items.example: To have oneself in hand is to control one's conduct.
items.exampleCN: 把自己握在手里，就是控制自己的举止。

items.example: The observers recorded the animal's behavior.
items.exampleCN: 观察者记录了这只动物的行为。

items.meaning: to act in a certain way
items.example: The children behaved well.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们表现很好。

items.example: Behavioral studies need clear definitions.
items.exampleCN: 行为研究需要清晰的定义。

items.example: The two groups differ behaviorally.
items.exampleCN: 两组在行为上存在差异。

items.meaning: the school that studies observable response
items.meaningCN: 研究可观察反应的行为主义
items.example: Behaviorism dominated psychology for decades.
items.exampleCN: 行为主义主导心理学数十年。

items.example: The teacher noted the misbehavior at once.
items.exampleCN: 老师立刻记下了这一不当行为。

items.example: British journals print behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 英国期刊写作 behaviour。

definition_zh: 行为的；行为方面的；行为主义的；以外在表现为依据的
definition_en: relating to behavior, or concerned with what can be observed rather than with inner states
core_image: 两台摄像机只拍下一个人做了什么，不拍他心里想了什么，屏幕上全是动作的轨迹
scene: 同样的光照照到两组小鼠，一组被放进迷宫，一组只是被称重，研究者比较的正是它们对同一提示作出的可见反应差异。 The two groups differ only in the visible responses they make to the same light cue, so the comparison is purely behavioral.
sceneCN: 这里 behavioral 指「属于行为层面、以可见反应为准的」（第 1 个义项：与行为有关的）；句意为两组的差别只在于对同一光提示作出的可见反应，因此比较纯属行为层面。可辨识物件：迷宫、鼠笼、称重台、光提示灯。

pos.zh: 行为主义的；只研究可观察反应的

derivatives.zh: 行为主义者；行为主义的

senses.title: Relating to behavior
senses.definition: concerned with the actions and reactions of a person, animal or system
senses.definitionCN: 涉及人、动物或系统的动作与反应
senses.example: The clinic treats behavioral problems in young children.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所处理幼儿的行为问题。
senses.why: Adding -al to behavior turns the noun into a label for anything that belongs to that domain, exactly as nation becomes national.
senses.whyCN: 给 behavior 加 -al，把名词变成标示「属于这一领域」的形容词，正如 nation 变 national。

senses.title: Based on observable response
senses.titleCN: 以可观察反应为依据的
senses.definition: measured or defined by what can be seen and recorded from outside
senses.definitionCN: 以从外部可见、可记录的内容来测量或定义
senses.example: The diagnosis rests on behavioral evidence, not on self-report.
senses.exampleCN: 该诊断依据行为证据，而非自我陈述。
senses.why: Psychology needed an adjective that keeps to the visible surface, so behavioral marks studies that refuse to guess at inner states.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要一个只停留在可见表面的形容词，因此 behavioral 标示那些拒绝猜度内在状态的研究。

senses.title: Belonging to behaviorism
senses.definition: of or according to the psychological school that explains behavior by stimulus and response
senses.definitionCN: 属于或依据以刺激—反应解释行为的那一心理学流派
senses.example: Behavioral models predict the press of a lever, not a change of mood.
senses.exampleCN: 行为主义模型预测的是按杆动作，而非情绪变化。
senses.why: Because behaviorism took behavior as its whole subject, its adjective became a label for a whole approach to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 因为行为主义把行为当作全部研究对象，其形容词就成了整套心智研究取向的标签。

senses.title: Of animal behavior as a field
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of what animals do
senses.definitionCN: 与科学地研究动物做什么有关
senses.example: Behavioral ecology asks why a bird defends a territory.
senses.exampleCN: 行为生态学追问鸟为什么守卫领地。
senses.why: Once the study of conduct became a discipline, its compound names needed an adjective to mark the behavioral half of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 一旦举止研究成为学科，其复合名称就需要一个形容词来标出课题中属于行为的那一半。

senses.title: Clinical: aimed at changing conduct
senses.titleCN: 临床意义上以改变行为为目标
senses.definition: describing treatment that works on actions rather than on insight alone
senses.definitionCN: 形容治疗直接作用于行动，而非只求领悟
senses.example: Behavioral therapy pairs a feared object with a calm response.
senses.exampleCN: 行为疗法把令人恐惧的物件与平静反应配对。
senses.why: If behavior can be measured, it can be trained; the adjective then names treatments that practise actions instead of discussing them.
senses.whyCN: 行为既然可测量，就可训练；这个形容词于是命名那些练习动作、而非讨论动作的疗法。

senses.title: Managerial: of conduct in organizations
senses.titleCN: 管理学中关于组织内行为的
senses.definition: relating to how people act within organizations, markets or groups
senses.definitionCN: 关于人在组织、市场或群体中如何行动
senses.example: Behavioral economics studies why buyers ignore the cheaper option.
senses.exampleCN: 行为经济学研究买者为何忽略更便宜的选项。
senses.why: The same adjective extends from individuals to aggregates, naming research on how groups and markets actually act.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词从个体扩展到集合体，命名关于群体与市场实际如何行动的研究。

senses.title: Defined by behavior rather than structure
senses.titleCN: 以行为而非结构来定义的
senses.definition: classified by what something does rather than by its anatomy or design
senses.definitionCN: 按某物做什么来分类，而非按其构造或设计
senses.example: The two species are behaviorally distinct though almost identical in form.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种外表几乎相同，行为上却可区分。
senses.why: Where structure fails to separate things, conduct can, so behavioral becomes a way of drawing a line between look-alikes.
senses.whyCN: 当结构无法区分事物时，行为可以，因此 behavioral 成了在形似之物间划线的方式。

senses.title: Abstract: surface-level only
senses.definition: used of an account that stays on the surface of what is done and says nothing about meaning
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容只停在「做了什么」的表面、不涉及意义的说法
senses.example: His apology was behavioral, a set of gestures with nothing behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉只是行为层面的，一串动作背后空无一物。
senses.why: At its widest, behavioral can criticize as well as describe: an account that never leaves the surface is called merely behavioral.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，behavioral 既能描述也能批评：始终不离表面的说法就被称为「只是行为层面的」。

intro.en: Behavioral is behavior plus the adjective suffix -al. The suffix is Latin in origin, but the base is a native English verb, so the word is a hybrid rather than a Latin derivative.
intro.cn: behavioral 是 behavior 加形容词后缀 -al。后缀源自拉丁语，词基却是英语本族动词，因此这个词是混合体，而非拉丁派生词。

items.en: Behave, from be- plus have, supplied the noun behavior in the late fifteenth century, and the adjective was built on that noun.
items.cn: behave 由 be- 加 have 构成，在 15 世纪晚期给出名词 behavior，形容词又建立在该名词上。

items.en: Latin -alis formed adjectives of relation, as in nationalis; English -al does the same, producing behavioral, national and natural.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 构成表关系的形容词，如 nationalis；英语 -al 作用相同，产生 behavioral、national 与 natural。

items.en: The adjective is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when psychology and the social sciences began naming their subfields.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词出现于 19 世纪，正值心理学与社会科学开始给自己的子领域命名。

items.en: Early twentieth-century behaviorism fixed behavioral as the adjective of an entire school, and compounds such as behavioral science followed.
items.cn: 20 世纪早期的行为主义把 behavioral 固定为整个学派的形容词，行为科学一类复合词随之出现。

items.en: British usage writes behavioural; the American form keeps the shorter behavior.
items.cn: 英式用法写作 behavioural；美式形式保留较短的 behavior。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation for behavioral is not fixed across dictionaries, and the derived adverb behaviorally appears later still, so both dates should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各词典对 behavioral 的最早书证并不统一，其派生副词 behaviorally 出现更晚，因此这两个年代都应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the spelling and family variants that students mix up; group two holds adjectives that also describe conduct but from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组区分学生常混的拼写与词族变体；第二组是同样描述举止、但角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The British form of the same adjective, identical in meaning and differing only in the u.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的英式形式，意义相同，只差一个字母 u。

entries.definition: The noun from which the adjective is built; it names the conduct, while the adjective labels the domain.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该形容词的名词；名词命名举止本身，形容词标示所属领域。

entries.definition: A person who follows behaviorism, or the adjective 'of behaviorism'; it names a practitioner, not a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 信奉行为主义的人，或「行为主义的」形容词；它命名从业者，而非表关系。

entries.definition: From be- plus fuddle, of obscure origin; it means confused and has no connection with behave.
entries.definitionCN: 由 be- 加来源不明的 fuddle 构成，意为糊涂，与 behave 无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind and inner states; it is the opposite direction from behavioral, which stays outside.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及心智与内在状态；与只停留在外部的 behavioral 方向相反。

entries.definition: Able to be seen or recorded; it states visibility itself, while behavioral states the domain.
entries.definitionCN: 可被看见或记录；它陈述可见性本身，behavioral 陈述领域。

entries.definition: Concerned with how something works rather than how it is built; from Latin fungi 'to perform'.
entries.definitionCN: 关注某物如何运作而非如何构成；来自拉丁 fungi「履行」。

entries.definition: Relating to groups and interaction; behavioral may be social or solitary, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及群体与互动；behavioral 既可社会性也可独处性，因此两者不能互换。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: behavior + -al: the adjective simply means 'of behavior'.
normal.cn: behavior + -al：这个形容词就是「行为方面的」。

normal.en: The family runs behavior, behavioral, behaviorally, behaviorism, behaviorist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 behavior、behavioral、behaviorally、behaviorism、behaviorist。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: behavioral science, behavioral economics, behavioral ecology, behavioral therapy.
normal.cn: 固定复合词：行为科学、行为经济学、行为生态学、行为疗法。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the u: behavioural.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 u：behavioural。

normal.en: Behaviorally usually stands at the end or before an adjective: behaviorally distinct, differ behaviorally.
normal.cn: behaviorally 常置于句末或形容词前：行为上可区分、在行为上有差异。

abstract.en: Picture a camera that films the hands but cannot film the intention.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只拍手、拍不到意图的摄影机。

abstract.en: Picture two identical keys that open different doors only because of how they are turned.
abstract.cn: 想象两把一模一样的钥匙，只因转动方式不同而打开不同的门。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of footsteps with no names attached to the walkers.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只画脚印、不标行走者姓名的图表。

examples.en: The grant supports behavioral research on memory and sleep.
examples.cn: 这笔资助支持关于记忆与睡眠的行为研究。

examples.en: Behavioral economists watch what people choose, not what they say.
examples.cn: 行为经济学家看人们选了什么，而不是说了什么。

examples.en: The two populations are behaviorally distinct during the breeding season.
examples.cn: 这两个群体在繁殖季的行为表现可区分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「behavior（行为）+ al（……的）」——只谈看得见的行为，不谈心里怎么想 → 行为的、行为主义的

root: behavior（behave：be- + have「把握自己」）+ -al（拉丁 -alis，表关系）；词基为本族英语，后缀为拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a plain 'of behavior' label to increasingly technical uses: observable surface, a whole school, a field, a therapy, a market, a diagnostic line, and finally a criticism of shallowness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从平实的「行为方面的」标签，走向越来越专门的用法：可见表面、整个学派、一个领域、一种疗法、一个市场、一条鉴别界线，最后是对浅薄的批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera that records only what is done and never what is meant.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台只记录做了什么、从不记录意味什么的摄影机。

branches.en: DOMAIN LABEL: the plain relation, and the use of conduct to separate near-identical forms.
branches.cn: 领域标签：平实的关系义，以及用行为区分外形几乎相同的类型。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE SURFACE: a methodological rule that hardens into a named school.
branches.cn: 可见表面：一条方法规则，硬化为一个有名字的学派。

branches.en: ORGANIZED STUDY: a discipline and its applied wing in markets and organizations.
branches.cn: 有组织的研究：一门学科及其在市场与组织中的应用分支。

branches.en: TRAINING CONDUCT: if it can be measured, it can be practised into shape.
branches.cn: 训练举止：既然可测量，就能练成形。

branches.en: CRITICAL EDGE: a surface account that never reaches meaning.
branches.cn: 批评的边缘：始终触不到意义的表面说法。

intro.en: Behavioral is a hybrid: a native English noun with a Latin-derived suffix. Both halves are common enough to be read separately.
intro.cn: behavioral 是混合词：本族英语名词加拉丁来源后缀。两半都足够常见，可以分开来读。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin: -alis 'relating to'. The base behavior is Germanic, and habere is not its source; the distant Latin cognate at PIE level is capere.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁语：-alis「与……相关」。词基 behavior 属日耳曼语，habere 并非其来源；在印欧层面遥远的拉丁同族是 capere。

items.example: The adjective describes a domain of behavior.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述行为这一领域。

items.example: Nation and national, nature and natural follow the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: nation 与 national、nature 与 natural 遵循同一模式。

items.example: The study used behavioral measures.
items.exampleCN: 该研究采用了行为测量。

items.example: The species differ behaviorally.
items.exampleCN: 这些物种在行为上不同。

items.example: British clinics offer behavioural therapy.
items.exampleCN: 英国诊所提供行为疗法。

items.meaning: one who studies or follows behaviorism
items.meaningCN: 研究或信奉行为主义的人
items.example: The behaviorist counts presses of a lever.
items.exampleCN: 行为主义者数按杆的次数。

items.meaningCN: 研究可观察反应的行为主义
items.example: Behaviorism shaped mid-century psychology.
items.exampleCN: 行为主义塑造了 20 世纪中叶的心理学。

items.example: The paper compares behavioral and nonbehavioral explanations.
items.exampleCN: 该论文比较了行为层面与非行为层面的解释。

items.example: Neurobehavioral tests track both reflex and conduct.
items.exampleCN: 神经行为测试同时追踪反射与举止。

definition_zh: 行为生态学：研究动物行为如何被生态环境塑造、又如何反过来影响生存与繁殖的分支学科
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies how ecological conditions shape animal behavior and how that behavior in turn affects survival and reproduction
core_image: 一只鸟在食物稀少的年份把觅食范围画得很大，在丰收年份又缩回巢边，地图上的圈随年景一张一缩
scene: 同一种鸟在食物稀少的年份扩大觅食范围，在食物充足时缩短，研究者据此统计每种策略留下的后代数量。 The team counts how many offspring each strategy yields and asks why the bird widens its search only when food is scarce, a standard question in behavioral ecology.
sceneCN: 这里 behavioral ecology 指「研究行为与生态环境相互作用的学科」（第 1 个义项：作为学科名）；句意为研究者统计不同觅食策略留下的后代数量，并追问鸟为何只在食物稀少时扩大搜索范围，这是行为生态学的典型问题。可辨识物件：逐年变化的觅食圈、巢、幼鸟、记录表。

pos.zh: 行为生态学（学科名，不可数）
（具体研究）行为生态学分析；行为与生态关系的考察

collocations.zh: 行为生态学中的一个问题

forms.label: 复数（多种行为生态学研究）

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为一门学科的行为生态学
senses.definition: the subfield of biology that joins the study of behavior to the study of ecological conditions
senses.definitionCN: 把行为研究与生态条件研究结合起来的生物学分支
senses.example: Behavioral ecology grew rapidly after the 1960s.
senses.exampleCN: 行为生态学在 20 世纪 60 年代后迅速发展。
senses.why: The compound names exactly what it joins: one half supplies the conduct, the other the environment in which that conduct must pay off.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词精确命名了它所连接的两半：一半提供行为，另一半提供行为必须在此获得回报的环境。

senses.title: The central question of adaptive value
senses.titleCN: 核心问题：行为的适应价值
senses.definition: the question of how a behavior raises or lowers an animal's chances of surviving and reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 某种行为如何提高或降低动物存活与繁殖机会的问题
senses.example: The paper asks the central behavioral ecology question: what does the display cost, and what does it buy?
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文提出行为生态学的核心问题：这种展示付出什么代价，又换回什么。
senses.why: Ecology supplies the currency, survival and offspring; behavior is then judged by what it earns in that currency.
senses.whyCN: 生态学提供货币，即存活与后代；行为则按它在这种货币中赚到什么来评判。

senses.title: A research programme treating behavior as a trait
senses.titleCN: 把行为当作性状的研究纲领
senses.definition: an approach that treats a behavior as a biological trait shaped by selection, like a beak or a wing
senses.definitionCN: 把某种行为当作受选择塑造的生物性状，如同喙或翅膀
senses.example: Treating nest defense as a trait changed how the team designed its experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 把护巢当作一种性状，改变了研究组设计实验的方式。
senses.why: If a behavior can be inherited and selected, it can be measured like any other trait, which is the move that made the field possible.
senses.whyCN: 既然行为可以遗传并被选择，它就能像别的性状一样被测量，正是这一步使这门学科成为可能。

senses.title: Analysis of behavioral strategies
senses.definition: the comparison of alternative strategies an animal might adopt under given conditions
senses.definitionCN: 对动物在给定条件下可能采取的各种替代策略的比较
senses.example: The model compares two foraging strategies under the same rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型比较同一降雨条件下的两种觅食策略。
senses.why: Once behavior is a trait, variants of it can be lined up as options, and the field asks which option pays best where.
senses.whyCN: 一旦行为成为性状，它的各种变体就能排成选项，这门学科便追问在何处哪个选项回报最高。

senses.title: Interface with population ecology
senses.definition: the study of how individual behavior changes birth rates, death rates and population size
senses.definitionCN: 个体行为如何改变出生率、死亡率与种群规模的研究
senses.example: Territory size links behavioral ecology to population ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 领地大小把行为生态学与种群生态学连接起来。
senses.why: When many individuals behave in the same way, their choices add up to births and deaths, so the field borders population ecology.
senses.whyCN: 当许多个体以同样方式行动，其选择就累加成出生与死亡，这门学科因此与种群生态学接壤。

senses.title: Interface with evolutionary biology
senses.definition: the study of how behavior evolves and how evolutionary history constrains it
senses.definitionCN: 行为如何进化、进化历史又如何限制行为的研究
senses.example: Comparative work places the dance of one species beside that of its relatives.
senses.exampleCN: 比较研究把某一物种的舞蹈与近缘物种的舞蹈并置。
senses.why: A trait that pays off is inherited, so the field must ask about ancestry as well as about present conditions.
senses.whyCN: 能带来回报的性状会被继承，因此这门学科既要问当下的条件，也要问祖先的来源。

senses.title: Application in conservation
senses.titleCN: 在保护生物学中的应用
senses.definition: the use of behavioral findings to plan reserves, reintroductions and wildlife management
senses.definitionCN: 用行为研究的发现来规划保护区、再引入与野生动物管理
senses.example: Behavioral ecology guided where the corridor was placed.
senses.exampleCN: 行为生态学指导了廊道的选址。
senses.why: If animals avoid a gap or refuse a new site, the map of a reserve must include their conduct, not only the habitat's area.
senses.whyCN: 如果动物回避某处空隙或拒绝新地点，保护区的图就必须纳入它们的举止，而不只是栖息地面积。

senses.title: Abstract: any behavior-environment analysis
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何「行为—环境」互动分析
senses.definition: any framework that reads conduct as an answer to environmental conditions, even outside biology
senses.definitionCN: 任何把举止读作对环境条件的回答的框架，即便在生物学之外
senses.example: The author applies behavioral ecology to how shoppers move through a market.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把行为生态学用于分析顾客如何在市场里移动。
senses.why: At its widest the compound becomes a template: any agent whose choices are shaped by scarce resources can be read this way.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个复合词成了一个模板：任何选择受稀缺资源塑造的主体都能这样解读。

intro.en: Behavioral ecology joins an English noun to a Greek-derived one. Behavior is native, from behave; ecology was coined in the nineteenth century from Greek oikos 'house, household' plus -logia 'study'.
intro.cn: behavioral ecology 把一个英语名词与一个希腊来源的名词结合起来。behavior 属本族语，来自 behave；ecology 是 19 世纪用希腊 oikos「家、居所」加 -logia「研究」造出的词。

items.en: Behavior dates from the late fifteenth century, from behave, literally 'to carry oneself'. It supplies the conduct half of the compound.
items.cn: behavior 自 15 世纪晚期出现，来自 behave，字面为「把握自己」，为复合词提供「行为」这一半。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household, dwelling place', the root of economy as well as of ecology.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家户、居所」，既是 economy 也是 ecology 的词根。

items.en: Ernst Haeckel coined German Oekologie in 1866 from oikos plus -logia, and English ecology followed in the same decade.
items.cn: 恩斯特·海克尔于 1866 年用 oikos 加 -logia 造出德语 Oekologie，英语 ecology 在同一十年随之出现。

items.en: The compound behavioral ecology is generally dated to the mid-twentieth century, when the two fields were deliberately joined.
items.cn: behavioral ecology 这一复合词一般认为形成于 20 世纪中叶，当时这两个领域被有意地连接起来。

items.en: Journals and societies bearing the name appeared later in the century, fixing the compound as a discipline rather than a phrase.
items.cn: 以该名命名的期刊与学会在该世纪后段出现，使这个复合词固定为一门学科，而不再只是一个短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single earliest citation for the English compound is settled, and the exact first coining of the term is debated, so the century rather than a year is reliable.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个英语复合词的最早书证并无统一说法，术语最初由谁造出也有争论，因此可靠的只是世纪，而非具体年份。

note.en: Group one separates the parts and near-names of the compound; group two holds neighbouring disciplines that answer different questions about the same animals.
note.cn: 第一组区分这个复合词的组成部分与近似名称；第二组是邻近学科，对同样的动物回答不同的问题。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of behavior'; it names one half of the compound and cannot stand for the discipline by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「行为的」的形容词；它只命名复合词的一半，不能单独代表这门学科。

entries.definition: The study of organisms and their surroundings; joined to behavioral, it names the hybrid field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与其环境；与 behavioral 结合，才命名这门交叉学科。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior from Greek ēthos 'character'; it overlaps in subject but not in name or emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ēthos「性格」的动物行为研究；研究对象重叠，但名称与侧重不同。

entries.definition: The study of the biological basis of social behavior, closer to evolution than to ecology in its questions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会行为的生物学基础，其问题更靠近进化而非生态。

entries.definition: The study of how ecological conditions shape evolutionary change; behavioral ecology focuses on conduct within that frame.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生态条件如何塑造进化变化；行为生态学则在该框架内聚焦举止。

entries.definition: The study of births, deaths and numbers in a population; behavior enters it only through aggregated individual choices.
entries.definitionCN: 研究种群中的出生、死亡与数量；行为只能通过个体选择的累加进入其中。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior through controlled experiments and cross-species comparison, often indoors.
entries.definitionCN: 通过受控实验与跨物种比较研究动物行为，常在室内进行。

entries.definition: The school that explains behavior by stimulus and response; it is a method, not an ecological field.
entries.definitionCN: 以刺激—反应解释行为的学派；它是一套方法，而非生态学领域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: behavioral + ecology: conduct read against environment, two halves of one name.
normal.cn: behavioral + ecology：把举止放到环境里读，一个名字的两半。

normal.en: The family runs behavior, behavioral, ecology, behavioral ecologist, behavioural ecology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 behavior、behavioral、ecology、behavioral ecologist、behavioural ecology。

normal.en: Typical phrases: a question in behavioral ecology, behavioral ecology model, the rise of behavioral ecology.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：行为生态学中的一个问题、行为生态学模型、行为生态学的兴起。

normal.en: The Greek oikos 'house' in ecology is the same root as in economy.
normal.cn: ecology 中的希腊 oikos「家」与 economy 同根。

normal.en: The central currency is fitness: survival plus offspring.
normal.cn: 核心货币是适合度：存活加后代。

abstract.en: Picture a bird's search circle breathing in and out with the size of the harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟的觅食圈随收成大小一呼一吸。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every display is entered as cost on one side and offspring on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每次展示一边记代价，一边记后代。

abstract.en: Picture a market where the same behaviour is read as a response to scarcity.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，同样的举止被读作对稀缺的回应。

examples.en: Behavioral ecology explains the timing of migration as a response to food and risk.
examples.cn: 行为生态学把迁徙的时机解释为对食物与风险的反应。

examples.en: Her thesis sits at the border of behavioral ecology and population ecology.
examples.cn: 她的论文位于行为生态学与种群生态学的交界处。

examples.en: The course introduces behavioral ecology through a single breeding colony.
examples.cn: 这门课通过一个繁殖群体介绍行为生态学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「behavior（行为）+ ecology（生态）」——把行为放进环境里算账，看它换来多少生存与后代 → 行为生态学

root: behavior（本族语，be- + have）+ ecology（希腊 oikos「家」+ -logia「研究」，1866 年由海克尔造出）构成的学术复合词；无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the name of a discipline, through its central question and method, to its interfaces with neighbouring fields, its applications, and finally a general template for reading conduct against conditions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科名称出发，经其核心问题与方法，走到与邻近领域的交界、实际应用，最后落到把举止放到条件里读的一般模板。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a behavior plotted on the same map as the resources that make it pay.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一种行为画在与它收益相关的资源同一张地图上。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS QUESTION: a name, then the single question of what a behavior costs and earns.
branches.cn: 领域与问题：先是一个名字，再是行为付出什么、换回什么这唯一问题。

branches.en: MAKING BEHAVIOR MEASURABLE: treated as a trait, then lined up as alternative strategies.
branches.cn: 使行为可测量：先当作性状，再排成替代策略。

branches.en: TWO NEIGHBOURS: individual choices add up into populations, and inherited traits point back to ancestry.
branches.cn: 两个邻居：个体选择累加成种群，可继承的性状又指向祖先。

branches.en: APPLIED EDGE: conduct enters the map of a reserve.
branches.cn: 应用边缘：举止进入保护区的地图。

branches.en: GENERAL TEMPLATE: any agent whose choices answer scarcity.
branches.cn: 一般模板：任何其选择在回应稀缺的主体。

intro.en: The compound is built from two transparent pieces, each with its own history: a native English noun and a Greek-derived scientific term.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个透明的部分组成，每部分各有自己的历史：一个本族英语名词与一个希腊来源的科学术语。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: behavior is Germanic, and ecology is coined from Greek oikos and -logia. Latin supplied only the connective adjective suffix -al.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：behavior 属日耳曼语，ecology 由希腊 oikos 与 -logia 造出。拉丁语只提供了连接用的形容词后缀 -al。

items.example: The first half names what is studied.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分命名被研究的对象。

items.example: It turns the noun into the modifying adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成修饰用的形容词。

items.example: The same root appears in economy.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根也出现在 economy 中。

items.example: Biology and geology share it.
items.exampleCN: biology 与 geology 共用它。

items.meaning: the study of organisms and their surroundings
items.meaningCN: 研究生物与其环境的学科
items.example: Ecology was named in 1866.
items.exampleCN: ecology 于 1866 年被命名。

items.example: Behavioral ecology asks what a display earns.
items.exampleCN: 行为生态学追问一次展示换来什么。

items.example: The behavioral ecologist tagged forty nests.
items.exampleCN: 这位行为生态学家给四十个巢做了标记。

items.example: A behavioral-ecological approach links the two data sets.
items.exampleCN: 行为生态学取向把两组数据连接起来。

items.example: British departments list behavioural ecology.
items.exampleCN: 英国院系列出 behavioural ecology。

definition_zh: 动物行为学；行为学：在自然条件下系统研究动物行为的学科；（早期义）性格描写、模仿表演
definition_en: the scientific study of animal behavior, especially in natural conditions, and historically the art of portraying character
core_image: 黎明前，一个裹在伪装帐里的人一动不动地坐着，只用铅笔记录一只鸟每一次转身的先后顺序
scene: 天亮以前，观察者躲在伪装帐里记下每只鸟求偶动作的先后次序，完全不改变周围的条件。 Before dawn the observer sits in a blind and writes down the order of each bird's display, altering nothing in the habitat, which is the method that defines ethology.
sceneCN: 这里 ethology 指「在自然条件下系统观察动物行为的学科」（第 1 个义项：动物行为学）；句意为观察者在伪装帐中按顺序记下求偶动作、不改变环境，这正是该学科的方法。可辨识物件：伪装帐、望远镜、铅笔、正在展示的鸟。

pos.zh: 动物行为学；行为学（学科名，不可数）
（早期用法）性格描写；以模仿刻画性格的表演

collocations.zh: 动物行为学与比较心理学
