senses.title: The study of animal behavior
senses.titleCN: 动物行为学：在自然条件下研究动物行为的学科
senses.definition: the branch of zoology that studies behavior, especially as observed in natural conditions
senses.definitionCN: 动物学的分支，研究行为，尤其侧重自然条件下的观察
senses.example: Ethology began with long hours of watching animals that were not disturbed.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学始于长时间观察不被打扰的动物。
senses.why: The Greek root ēthos means character or habitual disposition, so the name promises an account of how an animal characteristically conducts itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 ēthos 意为性格或习惯性情，因此这个名字承诺给出动物典型行事的说明。

senses.title: The comparative tradition
senses.definition: the tradition that compares behavior across species in order to reconstruct its evolution
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较行为、以重建其进化的研究传统
senses.example: The classic ethology of the 1930s compared displays across bird families.
senses.exampleCN: 20 世纪 30 年代的经典行为学比较了不同鸟科的表现。
senses.why: If character is species-specific, it can be compared between species, and comparison was the method that gave the field its identity.
senses.whyCN: 如果性格因物种而异，就能在物种间比较；比较正是赋予这门学科身份的方法。

senses.title: Historical sense: character portrayal
senses.titleCN: 早期义：性格描写与模仿表演
senses.definition: the older, seventeenth-century sense of depicting character by mimicry or description
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪较早的义项：以模仿或描写刻画性格
senses.example: In the older sense, ethology belonged to the stage rather than to zoology.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的义项里，ethology 属于舞台而非动物学。
senses.why: The word entered English through Latin ethologia, a borrowing of Greek ēthologia 'character portrayal', long before it named a science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经拉丁 ethologia 进入英语，那是希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」的借词，远早于它成为科学名称。

senses.title: Study of instinct and fixed patterns
senses.titleCN: 对本能与固定动作模式的研究
senses.definition: the study of unlearned, stereotyped patterns and the signals that release them
senses.definitionCN: 对非学习的刻板模式及其释放信号的研究
senses.example: Ethology gave fixed action patterns their name and their evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学为固定动作模式提供了名称与证据。
senses.why: The early ethologists needed behaviour that could be recognised across individuals, and unlearned patterns supplied exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 早期行为学家需要可在个体间辨认的行为，而非学习的刻板模式恰好提供这一点。

senses.title: Contrast with laboratory psychology
senses.titleCN: 与实验室心理学的对照
senses.definition: the field defined by natural observation as against controlled indoor experiment
senses.definitionCN: 以自然观察为标志、与室内受控实验相对的领域
senses.example: Ethology trusts the field notebook; experimental psychology trusts the lever and the timer.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学信任野外记录本；实验心理学信任杠杆与计时器。
senses.why: Two ways of knowing the same animal grew side by side, and the name ethology marked the one that insists on the habitat.
senses.whyCN: 认识同一动物的两条道路并肩生长，ethology 这个名字标出了坚持栖息地的那一条。

senses.title: Method: field observation and individual recognition
senses.titleCN: 方法：野外观察与个体识别
senses.definition: the practice of identifying individuals and recording sequences without intervening
senses.definitionCN: 辨认个体并在不介入的情况下记录行为序列的做法
senses.example: The ethology of the troop depended on knowing every face.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的行为学依赖对每一张面孔的识别。
senses.why: A sequence is only evidence if the same individual is followed, so the method had to invent ways of telling animals apart.
senses.whyCN: 只有当同一个体被持续跟踪，序列才算证据，因此这套方法必须发明辨认动物的手段。

senses.title: Modern extension: cognition and welfare
senses.titleCN: 现代扩展：认知与动物福利
senses.definition: the contemporary extension of the field to animal cognition, emotion and welfare
senses.definitionCN: 该领域向动物认知、情绪与福利的当代扩展
senses.example: Modern ethology tests whether a captive animal can choose its own routine.
senses.exampleCN: 现代动物行为学检验圈养动物能否选择自己的日常安排。
senses.why: Once natural conduct is the standard, confinement can be judged by how much of that conduct it allows.
senses.whyCN: 一旦自然举止成为标准，圈养就能按它允许多少这类举止来评判。

senses.title: Abstract: systematic account of a disposition
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对某种习性的系统描述
senses.definition: any systematic description of the characteristic conduct of a group or type
senses.definitionCN: 对某一群体或类型的典型举止所作的任何系统描述
senses.example: The novelist offers an ethology of the office, not of animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家写的是一门办公室行为学，而非动物行为学。
senses.why: Because ēthos means character, the word can always be borrowed back from zoology to mean an account of how a kind of creature lives.
senses.whyCN: 因为 ēthos 意为性格，这个词总能从动物学借回来，指对某一类存在者生活方式的说明。

intro.en: Ethology comes from Latin ethologia, a borrowing of Greek ēthologia 'character portrayal', built on ēthos 'character, habit' plus -logia 'study, account'. Its zoological sense is a nineteenth-century narrowing.
intro.cn: ethology 来自拉丁 ethologia，那是希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」的借词，由 ēthos「性格、习惯」加 -logia「研究、叙述」构成。其动物学义是 19 世纪的收窄。

items.en: Ēthos meant 'habitual character and disposition, moral character, custom'. Its deeper origin is debated; it is often connected with the reflexive pronoun root *s(w)e-, but that link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ēthos 意为「习惯性的性格与性情、道德品格、习俗」。其更深来源有争论，常被联系到反身代词词根 *s(w)e-，但该联系属重构。

items.en: Ēthologia meant 'character portrayal', the art of depicting a person's disposition, with no reference to animals.
items.cn: ēthologia 意为「性格刻画」，即描绘一个人性情的技艺，与动物无关。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as ethologia, and it is this Latin form that passed into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 ethologia，正是这个拉丁形式传入了英语。

items.en: English ethology is recorded from the late seventeenth century meaning 'mimicry, the art of depicting character by gesture'.
items.cn: 英语 ethology 自 17 世纪晚期有记录，义为「模仿，以手势刻画性格的技艺」。

items.en: Mill used it in 1843 for the science of character formation, and by 1897 it named the zoological study of animal behavior.
items.cn: 密尔在 1843 年用它指性格形成的科学；到 1897 年，它已指动物行为的动物学研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of ēthos is not established, and the claim that it shares a root with ethics rests on the same reconstructed base, so both should be labelled reconstruction rather than fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ēthos 在希腊语之前的历史未获确证；说它与伦理学同根，依据的是同一个重构词基，因此两者都应标为重构而非事实。

note.en: Group one separates forms built on the same Greek root from a look-alike built on a different one; group two holds fields that study the same animals with other methods.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一希腊词根构成的形式与另一词根构成的形近词；第二组是用别的方法研究同样动物的领域。

entries.definition: The adjective from ethology, meaning 'of the study of animal behavior'.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ethology 构成的形容词，意为「动物行为学的」。

entries.definition: A person who practises ethology; the -ist suffix names the worker, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事动物行为学的人；-ist 后缀命名从业者，而非学科。

entries.definition: From Greek ēthikos 'of character', built on the same ēthos; it concerns moral conduct, not animal observation.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ēthikos「关于性格的」，建立在同一个 ēthos 上；它关乎道德行为，而非动物观察。

entries.definition: From Greek ethnos 'people' plus -logia: the comparative study of peoples, not of animal character.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ethnos「族群」加 -logia：对各民族的比较研究，而非动物性格。

entries.definition: The study of behavior as an answer to ecological conditions; ethology is older and more descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 把行为当作对生态条件的回答来研究；ethology 更早、更偏描述。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior by controlled experiment and cross-species comparison, often in laboratories.
entries.definitionCN: 通过受控实验与跨物种比较研究动物行为，常在实验室进行。

entries.definition: The study of the biological basis of social behavior, especially through inclusive fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会行为的生物学基础，尤其通过广义适合度。

entries.definition: A school explaining behavior by stimulus and response; it shares the word 'behavior' but not the field method.
entries.definitionCN: 以刺激—反应解释行为的学派；共用 behavior 一词，但不共用领域方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ēthos 'character' + -logia 'study': the study of how a creature characteristically lives.
normal.cn: ēthos「性格」+ -logia「研究」：研究一种生物如何按其性格生活。

normal.en: The family runs ethology, ethological, ethologically, ethologist, ethogram.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ethology、ethological、ethologically、ethologist、ethogram。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field ethology, the rise of ethology, a classic of ethology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外行为学、行为学的兴起、行为学经典著作。

normal.en: Ethics shares the Greek root ēthos but concerns moral conduct.
normal.cn: 伦理学共用希腊词根 ēthos，但关乎道德行为。

normal.en: The classic method is the blind, the notebook and the identified individual.
normal.cn: 经典方法是伪装帐、记录本与已识别的个体。

abstract.en: Picture a watcher who becomes furniture so the animals forget the watcher.
abstract.cn: 想象观察者变成家具，让动物忘了他。

abstract.en: Picture a species' whole temperament written out as a list of ordered acts.
abstract.cn: 想象把一个物种的全部性情写成一张按序排列的动作清单。

abstract.en: Picture the same word borrowed back to describe the habits of an office.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词被借回来描述一间办公室的习气。

examples.en: Ethology insists that behavior be described before it is explained.
examples.cn: 动物行为学坚持先描述行为，再解释行为。

examples.en: Her fieldwork became a classic of ethology.
examples.cn: 她的野外工作成了行为学经典。

examples.en: The old sense of ethology survives in essays on stage mimicry.
examples.cn: ethology 的旧义仍残存在论舞台模仿的文章里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「etho（性格/习性）+ logy（学）」——研究动物天生习性的一门学问 → 动物行为学

root: 希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」= ēthos（性格、习惯）+ -logia（研究、叙述）；经拉丁 ethologia 进入英语，动物学义为 19 世纪收窄；希腊语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one word from a stage art, through a nineteenth-century science of character, into field observation, then out again into cognition, welfare and any account of a characteristic way of living.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个词：从舞台技艺，到 19 世纪的性格科学，进入野外观察，再扩展至认知、福利，最后到任何关于典型生活方式的描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unobtrusive watcher writing down the order of what an animal does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个不引人注意的观察者，记下动物动作的先后顺序。

branches.en: WATCHING WELL: the discipline and the method that identifies individuals and keeps hands off.
branches.cn: 好好观察：学科本身，以及辨认个体、不加干预的方法。

branches.en: PATTERNS COMPARED: species are set beside species, and unlearned patterns give the comparison solid units.
branches.cn: 被比较的模式：物种与物种并置，非学习的模式为比较提供坚实单位。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: character portrayal, still visible when the word is borrowed back.
branches.cn: 旧义：性格刻画，当这个词被借回时仍可见。

branches.en: TWO WAYS OF KNOWING: the field notebook against the lever and the timer.
branches.cn: 两种认识方式：野外记录本对杠杆与计时器。

branches.en: FROM ANIMALS TO ANY CHARACTER: welfare today, and any systematic account of a disposition at the widest.
branches.cn: 从动物到任何性格：今日的福利研究，以及在最宽处对任何性情的系统描述。

intro.en: Ethology is a Greek compound that reached English through Latin, so each of its pieces has a clear history even though the word looks opaque.
intro.cn: ethology 是一个经拉丁语传入英语的希腊复合词，因此尽管词形看似难解，每个部分都有清楚的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributed the borrowed form ethologia, but no Latin root; the pieces are Greek ēthos and -logia. Since there is no Latin cognate family, no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了借词形式 ethologia，但未贡献词根；两个部分都是希腊语 ēthos 与 -logia。由于没有拉丁同族词族，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The first element names what is portrayed or studied.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分命名被刻画或研究的对象。

items.example: Biology and ethnology use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: biology 与 ethnology 使用同一后缀。

items.meaning: the study of animal character and behavior
items.meaningCN: 研究动物性格与行为的学科
items.example: Ethology grew out of natural history.
items.exampleCN: ethology 从博物学中生长出来。

items.example: The ethological literature is full of sequence diagrams.
items.exampleCN: 行为学文献里满是序列图。

items.meaning: from an ethological point of view
items.example: Ethologically, the two calls are distinct.
items.exampleCN: 从行为学上看，这两种叫声不同。

items.example: The ethologist spent a year in the canopy.
items.exampleCN: 这位行为学家在树冠层待了一年。

items.example: The ethogram lists forty distinct acts.
items.exampleCN: 行为谱列出四十种不同的动作。

items.meaning: the character of a people or group
items.meaningCN: 群体或民族的精神气质
items.example: The ethos of the group shaped its gestures.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体的气质塑造了它的手势。

items.example: Ethnology is a different field built on a different root.
items.exampleCN: ethnology 是建立在另一个词根上的不同领域。

definition_zh: 动物行为学的；行为学意义上的；以自然条件下可观察举止为依据的
definition_en: relating to ethology, or based on the descriptive study of animal behavior in natural conditions
core_image: 一段录像被放慢十倍，两只动物之间的每个动作都被编号，争论停止，只剩顺序表
scene: 两位研究者不再争论动作背后的内在原因，只比对野外记录下来的先后与频率，最后得出一个行为学层面的结论。 Rather than argue about hidden causes, the two researchers compare the recorded order and frequency of the movements and reach an ethological conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 ethological 指「属于动物行为学方法、以可观察举止为依据的」（第 1 个义项：行为学的）；句意为两人不再争论内在原因，只比对野外记录的先后与频率，得出行为学层面的结论。可辨识物件：放慢的录像、编号标签、频率表、野外记录本。

pos.zh: 动物行为学的；行为学意义上的
以自然观察为依据的（方法层面）
描述性的；先记录后解释的

senses.title: Belonging to ethology
senses.definition: of or belonging to the scientific study of animal behavior
senses.definitionCN: 属于动物行为这一科学研究的
senses.example: The journal publishes ethological work alongside physiology.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊把行为学研究与生理学研究并列发表。
senses.why: The suffix -ical turns the discipline's name into an adjective of relation, so the word marks a piece of work as belonging to that field.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ical 把学科名变成表关系的形容词，因此这个词把一项工作标为属于该领域。

senses.title: Based on natural observation
senses.definition: resting on records made in the animal's own habitat rather than in an enclosure
senses.definitionCN: 依据在动物自身栖息地而非围栏中作出的记录
senses.example: Their ethological data came from three seasons in the same valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的行为学数据来自在同一山谷的三个季节。
senses.why: The discipline was built on watching undisturbed animals, so its adjective carries that condition as part of its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科建立在观察未受干扰的动物之上，因此其形容词把这一条件当作词义的一部分。

senses.title: Descriptive before explanatory
senses.definition: describing what is done and in what order before assigning any cause
senses.definitionCN: 先描述做了什么、以什么次序，再谈任何原因
senses.example: An ethological account of the fight lists the moves before naming the hormone.
senses.exampleCN: 对这场争斗的行为学描述先列出动作，再提激素。
senses.why: The early field insisted that a catalogue of acts must exist before theories of motivation, and the adjective keeps that order.
senses.whyCN: 早期研究者坚持必须先有动作清单，才谈动机理论，这个形容词保留了那个次序。

senses.title: Comparative across species
senses.definition: comparing the behavior of different species in order to infer relationships
senses.definitionCN: 比较不同物种的行为以推断亲缘关系
senses.example: The ethological comparison placed the two courtship dances side by side.
senses.exampleCN: 行为学比较把两种求偶舞并排放置。
senses.why: If conduct is species-specific, it can serve as a character in a comparison, exactly as a bone does in anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 如果举止因物种而异，它就能像解剖学中的骨头一样，成为比较中的一项特征。

senses.title: Of fixed action patterns
senses.definition: describing unlearned, stereotyped movements released by a specific sign
senses.definitionCN: 描述由特定信号释放、非学习的刻板动作
senses.example: The ethological term for the sequence is a fixed action pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这一序列的行为学术语是固定动作模式。
senses.why: The field's most famous units were these rigid sequences, so the adjective often signals that a pattern is unlearned and repeatable.
senses.whyCN: 该领域最著名的单位就是这些刻板序列，因此这个形容词常暗示某模式是非学习且可重复的。

senses.title: Framed by evolutionary explanation
senses.definition: asking how a behavior arose and what advantage it gave in ancestral conditions
senses.definitionCN: 追问某行为如何产生、在祖先环境中带来什么优势
senses.example: The ethological question is not whether the bird feels fear but why fear pays.
senses.exampleCN: 行为学的问题不是鸟是否感到恐惧，而是恐惧为何划算。
senses.why: Once a behavior is a trait, it has a history, and the adjective marks explanations that ask about that history rather than about mechanism alone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦行为成为性状，它就有历史；这个形容词标示那些追问历史、而非只问机制的说明。

senses.title: As a welfare indicator
senses.definition: using observed behavior as a measure of an animal's condition in captivity
senses.definitionCN: 以观察到的行为衡量圈养动物的处境
senses.example: Pacing is an ethological warning sign in this species.
senses.exampleCN: 对这一物种来说，来回踱步是行为学上的警示信号。
senses.why: If natural conduct is the standard, then abnormal conduct can be read as evidence of a poor environment, which is how the adjective entered welfare science.
senses.whyCN: 如果自然举止是标准，那么异常举止就能被读作环境不良的证据，这个形容词正是这样进入福利科学的。

senses.title: Abstract: judged only from observable conduct
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：仅凭可观察举止判断的
senses.definition: used of any judgement that stays with what can be seen and refuses to speculate about inner life
senses.definitionCN: 用于任何只停留在可见之物、拒绝揣测内在生活的判断
senses.example: His portrait of the two brothers is ethological, all gesture and no confession.
senses.exampleCN: 他对两兄弟的刻画是行为学的，全是手势，没有一句自白。
senses.why: At its widest the adjective describes a way of knowing, one that trusts conduct over testimony.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个形容词描述一种认识方式：信任举止，胜过信任自述。

intro.en: Ethological is the adjective of ethology, built with the suffix -ical on the Greek-derived noun. It appears in English in the nineteenth century, when the discipline itself was being named.
intro.cn: ethological 是 ethology 的形容词，由希腊来源的名词加后缀 -ical 构成。它在 19 世纪出现，正值这门学科本身获得名称。

items.en: The base is ēthos 'character, habit', the same root that gives ethics; it names disposition rather than moral rules.
items.cn: 词基是 ēthos「性格、习惯」，也是伦理学的词根；它命名的是性情，而非道德规则。

items.en: -Logia 'study, account' made ēthologia 'character portrayal', which Latin borrowed as ethologia.
items.cn: -logia「研究、叙述」构成 ēthologia「性格刻画」，拉丁语借作 ethologia。

items.en: English ethology is recorded from the late seventeenth century; its zoological sense was fixed at the end of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 ethology 自 17 世纪晚期有记录；其动物学义在 19 世纪末固定下来。

items.en: The suffix -ical, from Latin -icalis, forms relational adjectives such as ethical and zoological, and the adjective appears with the rise of the science.
items.cn: 后缀 -ical 源自拉丁 -icalis，构成 ethical、zoological 一类关系形容词；这个形容词随该科学的兴起而出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective spread into welfare science and into any descriptive account of conduct.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个形容词扩散到福利科学，也扩散到任何对举止的描述性说明。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation for the English adjective is not fixed across dictionaries, and the pre-Greek history of ēthos remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个英语形容词的最早书证在各词典中并不统一；ēthos 在希腊语之前的历史仍属重构。

note.en: Group one separates family forms from look-alikes that use other roots; group two holds adjectives that also describe how knowledge of behavior is obtained.
note.cn: 第一组区分同族形式与使用别的词根的形近词；第二组是同样描述「行为知识如何获得」的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the adjective names work that belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；形容词命名属于该学科的工作。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the discipline, formed with -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 该学科的从业者，由 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: From the same Greek ēthos but through ēthikos 'of character': it concerns right conduct, not animal observation.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自希腊 ēthos，但经 ēthikos「关于性格的」：关乎正当行为，而非动物观察。

entries.definition: From ethnos 'people', not ēthos 'character': it belongs to the study of peoples.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ethnos「族群」而非 ēthos「性格」：属于民族研究。

entries.definition: Based on watching and recording; it states the method alone, without naming a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 以观看与记录为依据；只陈述方法，不命名学科。

entries.definition: Setting out what happens without explaining why; ethological work is often descriptive but not always.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述发生了什么而不解释原因；行为学工作常是描述性的，但并非总是。

entries.definition: Setting two or more cases side by side; the ethological tradition is comparative in exactly this sense.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个或更多案例并置；行为学传统正是在这个意义上比较。

entries.definition: Relating to behavior in general, including laboratory work; ethological is narrower and field-based.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与行为有关，包括实验室工作；ethological 更窄，且以野外为基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ethology + -ical: the adjective of the field.
normal.cn: ethology + -ical：这门学科的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs ethology, ethological, ethologically, ethologist, ethogram.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ethology、ethological、ethologically、ethologist、ethogram。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ethological approach, ethological evidence, ethological perspective.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：行为学取向、行为学证据、行为学视角。

normal.en: Ethical looks alike but speaks of right and wrong, not of animals.
normal.cn: ethical 形近，但讲的是对错，不是动物。

normal.en: The adverb is common in judgements: ethologically distinct, ethologically meaningless.
normal.cn: 副词常用于判断句：行为上可区分、行为学上没有意义。

abstract.en: Picture a debate silenced by a table of numbered movements.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论被一张编了号的动作表压住。

abstract.en: Picture a judge who refuses to hear confessions and only watches hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一位拒绝听自白、只看手的法官。

abstract.en: Picture an animal pacing in a cage while a checklist quietly fills up.
abstract.cn: 想象动物在笼中来回踱步，一张清单静静填满。

examples.en: The ethological literature describes the sequence before testing any hormone.
examples.cn: 行为学文献先描述这一序列，再检验任何激素。

examples.en: Their ethological approach kept the animals in their own valley.
examples.cn: 他们的行为学取向让动物留在自己的山谷里。

examples.en: Ethologically, the two calls serve different functions.
examples.cn: 从行为学上看，这两种叫声承担不同功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethology（行为学）+ ical（……的）」——按野外记录下来的动作下结论 → 行为学的

root: ethology（希腊 ēthos「性格」+ -logia「研究」，经拉丁 ethologia）+ -ical（拉丁 -icalis，表关系）；与 ethical 同根不同义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: on what grounds is this said? The adjective begins as a field label, then names a method, a descriptive order, a comparison, a unit, an evolutionary frame, a welfare standard and finally a way of knowing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：这话凭什么说？这个形容词先是领域标签，再命名方法、描述次序、比较、单位、进化框架、福利标准，最后是一种认识方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered list of movements standing in place of an argument about causes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张编号的动作清单，取代了关于原因的争论。

branches.en: FIELD AND EVIDENCE: the label of a discipline, and the kind of record it accepts.
branches.cn: 领域与证据：一个学科的标签，以及它接受的记录类型。

branches.en: ORDER AND COMPARISON: describe the sequence, then set species side by side.
branches.cn: 次序与比较：先描述序列，再把物种并置。

branches.en: UNITS AND HISTORY: fixed patterns give the comparison its units, and evolution gives it a direction.
branches.cn: 单位与历史：固定模式为比较提供单位，进化为其提供方向。

branches.en: APPLIED TEST: abnormal conduct read as evidence about a environment.
branches.cn: 应用检验：异常举止被读作关于环境的证据。

branches.en: WAY OF KNOWING: conduct trusted over testimony.
branches.cn: 认识方式：信任举止胜过信任自述。

intro.en: Ethological is a two-step derivative: a Greek compound noun, then a Latin relational suffix. Both steps are transparent.
intro.cn: ethological 是两步派生：先有希腊复合名词，再加拉丁关系后缀。两步都透明。

latinIntro.en: The noun came to English through Latin ethologia, but the root is Greek; Latin also supplied the suffix -icalis. No Latin cognate family exists, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 名词经拉丁 ethologia 进入英语，但词根是希腊语；拉丁语还提供了后缀 -icalis。不存在拉丁同族词族，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root names what is observed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被观察的东西。

items.example: Ethology and biology share it.
items.exampleCN: ethology 与 biology 共用它。

items.example: Ethical and zoological use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: ethical 与 zoological 使用同一后缀。

items.meaning: of the study of animal behavior
items.example: The ethological record is unusually complete.
items.exampleCN: 这份行为学记录异常完整。

items.example: The displays are ethologically equivalent.
items.exampleCN: 这些展示在行为学上等价。

items.example: The ethologist coded every video twice.
items.exampleCN: 这位行为学家把每段录像编码了两次。

items.example: The ethogram became the study's backbone.
items.exampleCN: 行为谱成了这项研究的骨架。

items.example: The paper separates ethological from non-ethological evidence.
items.exampleCN: 该论文区分行为学证据与非行为学证据。

items.meaningCN: 结合行为研究与环境的
items.example: An ethological-ecological reading links the two data sets.
items.exampleCN: 行为—生态的读法把两组数据连接起来。

definition_zh: 交流；沟通；信息传递；（通信）通讯；（传播学）传播
definition_en: the process of sharing information, ideas or feelings, or the message that is shared
core_image: 一只侦察蜂回巢后跳起摆尾舞，翅膀的震动把花的方向与距离交给整群蜂
scene: 侦察蜂回巢后跳起摆尾舞，摆动的角度与持续时间把蜜源的方向和距离告诉其他工蜂。 A scout returns and performs a waggle dance whose angle and duration send the other workers straight to the flowers, one of the clearest cases of animal communication.
sceneCN: 这里 communication 指「个体之间传递信息的过程」（第 6 个义项：动物之间的信号传递）；句意为侦察蜂用摆尾舞的角度与时长把蜜源方位告诉同伴，是动物信息传递最清楚的例子之一。可辨识物件：蜂巢、摆尾的蜜蜂、花丛、方向线。

pos.zh: 消息；信件；传达的信息（可数）

forms.label: 复数（多指消息、通信系统）
形容词（可传达的； communicable 指疾病可传染的）
形容词（健谈的；善于沟通的）

senses.title: The process of sharing meaning
senses.definition: the two-way process by which people or animals share information, ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物共享信息、想法或感受的双向过程
senses.example: Good communication depends on both sides checking what was heard.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的沟通依赖双方核对各自听到了什么。
senses.why: The Latin verb communicare meant 'to share, to make common', so the noun begins as the act of making something common to two parties.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 communicare 意为「分享、使共有」，因此这个名词最初就是把某物变为双方共有的动作。

senses.title: A message that is sent
senses.definition: a letter, note or piece of information that is sent to someone
senses.definitionCN: 寄给某人的信件、便条或一条信息
senses.example: The office received a communication from the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 该办公室收到部里来的一份公文。
senses.why: Once sharing is a process, its object can be counted, and English uses the same noun for the thing shared and for the sharing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦共享成为过程，其对象就可计数，英语便用同一个名词既指共享动作，也指被共享之物。

senses.title: Telecommunications technology
senses.definition: the technology and systems by which signals are transmitted over distance
senses.definitionCN: 把信号远距离传输的技术与系统
senses.example: The storm knocked out communication across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断了整个山谷的通讯。
senses.why: Modern technology extended 'making common' from words to signals, and the noun came to name the wires, waves and networks themselves.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术把「使共有」从言语扩展到信号，这个名词于是用来指线路、电波与网络本身。

senses.title: A mode of expression
senses.definition: the particular channel or style through which meaning is conveyed, such as speech, writing or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 传达意义所用的特定渠道或风格，如口语、书面或手势
senses.example: Written communication leaves no tone of voice to soften a sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 书面沟通没有语调可以缓和一句话。
senses.why: Because sharing needs a channel, the noun can name the channel itself, and the plural often covers several channels at once.
senses.whyCN: 因为共享需要渠道，这个名词就能命名渠道本身，复数形式常同时涵盖多种渠道。

senses.title: The academic field
senses.definition: the academic study of how messages are produced, transmitted and received
senses.definitionCN: 研究消息如何被生产、传输与接收的学科
senses.example: She teaches communication at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学教传播学。
senses.why: A process so central to society became an object of study, and the uncountable singular now names a department as well as an act.
senses.whyCN: 如此核心的社会过程成为研究对象，这个不可数单数形式如今既指动作，也指一个系。

senses.title: Signal transfer between animals
senses.definition: the sending and receiving of signals that change another animal's behavior
senses.definitionCN: 发送并接收能改变另一动物行为的信号
senses.example: The dance is communication only if the other bees change what they do.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当其他蜂改变了行为，这场舞才算信息传递。
senses.why: Biology defines communication by effect rather than intention: a signal counts when a receiver responds, which is why the concept works without words.
senses.whyCN: 生物学以效果而非意图定义信息传递：只有当接收者作出反应，信号才算数，这正是该概念无需言语也能成立的原因。

senses.title: Internal organizational communication
senses.definition: the flow of information within an institution, between levels and departments
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部各层级与各部门之间的信息流动
senses.example: Poor internal communication let two teams duplicate the same work.
senses.exampleCN: 内部沟通不畅让两个团队重复了同样的工作。
senses.why: Wherever many people must act as one, making information common becomes a managed function, and the noun names that function.
senses.whyCN: 只要许多人必须像一个人那样行动，使信息共有就成为一项被管理的职能，这个名词便命名该职能。

senses.title: Abstract: the making of a connection
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：建立连接、使彼此相通
senses.definition: any process by which two separated things are brought into a shared relation
senses.definitionCN: 任何把两个分离之物带入共有关系的过程
senses.example: The bridge is a communication between the two halves of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是城镇两半之间的通道。
senses.why: At its oldest and widest, the word needs no message at all: anything that makes a passage or a link can be called a communication.
senses.whyCN: 在其最古老、最宽泛的用法里，这个词完全不需要消息：任何造成通路或连接的东西都可称为 communication。

intro.en: Communication comes from Latin communicatio 'a sharing, imparting', from communicare 'to share, make common', built on communis 'common, shared'. It enters English in the late fourteenth century.
intro.cn: communication 来自拉丁 communicatio「分享、传达」，源自动词 communicare「分享、使共有」，后者建立在 communis「共同的、共有的」之上。它在 14 世纪晚期进入英语。

items.en: Communis meant 'common, public, shared by all or many'. Its deeper analysis is debated; it is generally taken as com- 'together' plus a form related to exchange or obligation, but that segmentation is a hypothesis.
items.cn: communis 意为「共同的、公共的、为众人所共有的」。其更深分析有争论；一般认为由 com-「共同」加一个与交换或义务有关的形式构成，但这一切分只是假说。

items.en: Communicare meant 'to share, to impart, to make common', and in classical use could also mean to join with someone.
items.cn: communicare 意为「分享、传达、使共有」，古典用法中也可指与某人结合。

items.en: The noun communicatio named the act of sharing or imparting, and later also a statement or a message.
items.cn: 名词 communicatio 命名分享或传达的动作，后来也指陈述或消息。

items.en: English communication is recorded from the late fourteenth century as 'the act of communicating, that which is communicated'.
items.cn: 英语 communication 自 14 世纪晚期有记录，义为「传达的动作、被传达之物」。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word named transport and telegraphy, and in the twentieth century it became the name of a discipline.
items.cn: 自 19 世纪起，这个词指运输与电报技术；到 20 世纪，它成为一门学科的名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin structure of communis is not settled, and the link sometimes drawn to munus 'duty, gift' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：communis 在拉丁语之前的结构未有定论；有人把它联系到 munus「义务、赠礼」，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one separates the family verbs and adjectives from a look-alike of another root; group two holds near synonyms that name different parts of the same event.
note.cn: 第一组区分同族动词、形容词与另一词根的形近词；第二组是近义词，命名同一事件的不同部分。

entries.definition: The verb 'to share or convey'; communication is the act or the thing conveyed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「分享或传达」；communication 是动作或被传达之物。

entries.definition: Describing a person or channel that conveys readily; it describes a disposition, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人或渠道乐于传达；描述一种倾向，而非过程。

entries.definition: From the same communis 'common': a group that holds things in common, not the act of sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 communis「共同」：一个共有事物的群体，而非分享的动作。

entries.definition: From Latin communio 'fellowship': a shared state, especially religious, rather than an exchange of messages.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 communio「团契」：一种共有的状态，尤指宗教上的，而非消息交换。

entries.definition: A sign that carries a message; communication is the system or process in which signals travel.
entries.definitionCN: 承载消息的符号；communication 是信号在其中传递的系统或过程。

entries.definition: The sending of something in one direction, from Latin transmittere; it lacks the idea of shared understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 某物朝一个方向的发送，来自拉丁 transmittere；缺少共同理解之意。

entries.definition: A giving and receiving in return; it stresses reciprocity rather than the making of a shared meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 给出并得到回报；强调相互性，而非共同意义的形成。

entries.definition: Letters exchanged between people; it is one channel of communication, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间往来的书信；它是 communication 的一个渠道，而非全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + communis 'common': making something common to two parties.
normal.cn: com-「共同」+ communis「共有」：把某物变为双方共有。

normal.en: The family runs communicate, communication, communicative, communicator, communicable, community.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 communicate、communication、communicative、communicator、communicable、community。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: communication skills, means of communication, mass communication, animal communication.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：沟通技巧、通信手段、大众传播、动物信息传递。

normal.en: The plural communications usually means systems or messages: the ministry's communications, telephone communications.
normal.cn: 复数 communications 通常指系统或消息：部里的公文、电话通讯。

normal.en: Biology counts communication by effect: the receiver must change what it does.
normal.cn: 生物学按效果计算信息传递：接收者必须改变行为。

abstract.en: Picture a dance that turns a flower's position into a direction every bee can fly.
abstract.cn: 想象一场舞把花的位置变成一个每只蜂都能飞的方向。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge across a river that carries nothing but still makes two sides one town.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，什么也不运，却仍让两岸成为一个城镇。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding one idea between them like a shared umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人共撑一把伞，中间是同一个想法。

examples.en: Clear communication prevents most of the mistakes we blame on others.
examples.cn: 清晰的沟通能避免我们把大多数错误归咎于他人。

examples.en: The bees' dance is communication because it changes where the others fly.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂的舞蹈属于信息传递，因为它改变了其他蜂飞往何处。

examples.en: The department of communication studies how messages reach audiences.
examples.cn: 传播学系研究消息如何抵达受众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「common（共同）+ ication（过程）」——把信息变成大家共同拥有的东西 → 交流、沟通、通信

root: 拉丁 communicatio「分享、传达」← communicare「使共有」← communis「共同的」；communis 的更深来源不确定，与 munus「义务、赠礼」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same movement outward: meaning is made common, then the message, the channel, the technology, the discipline, the animal signal, the organization, and finally any link at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个向外扩展的动作：先使意义共有，再到消息、渠道、技术、学科、动物信号、组织，最后到任何连接。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two separated parties holding one thing in common.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个分离的方面共同持有同一样东西。

branches.en: PROCESS AND OBJECT: the act of sharing, and the thing that is shared.
branches.cn: 过程与对象：分享的动作，以及被分享之物。

branches.en: MEANS OF REACHING: signals over distance, and the style or channel that carries them.
branches.cn: 抵达的手段：远距离信号，以及承载它们的风格或渠道。

branches.en: MADE INTO A DISCIPLINE: the process becomes an object of teaching and research.
branches.cn: 成为学科：过程本身成为教学与研究的对象。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: animals and institutions both share information without speech.
branches.cn: 超越言语：动物与机构都能不用言语地共享信息。

branches.en: OLDEST AND WIDEST: a passage or link that makes two things continuous.
branches.cn: 最古老也最宽：一条使两物连通的通路或连接。

intro.en: Communication is a Latin noun with a prefix, a root and two suffixes, and each piece recurs in familiar English words.
intro.cn: communication 是一个拉丁名词，含一个前缀、一个词根与两个后缀，每个部分都在熟悉的英语词中重现。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis 'common' gives community, communion and communication; communicare 'to make common' gives communicate and communicative; the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 communis「共同的」给出 community、communion 与 communication；communicare「使共有」给出 communicate 与 communicative；后缀 -ation 标示动作或其结果。

items.example: The prefix supplies the idea of two parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供「双方」的意思。

items.example: The root is the source of community.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是 community 的来源。

items.example: The verb underlies communicate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 communicate 的基础。

items.example: Communication can mean the act or the thing shared.
items.exampleCN: communication 既可指动作，也可指被共享之物。

items.example: The ministry sent a communication.
items.exampleCN: 部里发来一份公文。

items.example: They communicate by gesture.
items.exampleCN: 他们用手势交流。

items.example: She is a communicative teacher.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位善于沟通的老师。

items.example: A good communicator checks for misreading.
items.exampleCN: 好的传达者会核对误读。

items.example: The community shares one well.
items.exampleCN: 这个共同体共用一口井。

items.example: Some diseases are communicable.
items.exampleCN: 有些疾病会传染。

definition_zh: 发出信号；信号传递（过程）；（生物学）信号发送行为；（通信）信令
definition_en: the act or process of sending signals, especially as a system of communication
core_image: 夜里的池塘边，一只雄蛙鼓起鸣囊发声，邻近的雄蛙应声而答，声浪一圈圈向外推开
scene: 池塘边一只雄蛙鼓起鸣囊发声，邻近的雄蛙随即回应，声音在夜色中一层层传开。 At the pond edge one male inflates his vocal sac and calls, neighbours answer, and the sound spreads outward through the dark, a clear case of signaling.
sceneCN: 这里 signaling 指「发出信号并被接收的过程」（第 1 个义项：信号发送动作）；句意为雄蛙鸣叫、邻近雄蛙回应、声音层层传开，构成清楚的信号发送过程。可辨识物件：鼓起的鸣囊、池塘水面、夜色中的草丛、回应的另一只蛙。

pos.zh: 信号发送；信号传递（过程）
发出信号的；信号传导的（作定语，如信号通路）

collocations.zh: 诚实信号（信号可靠地反映品质）

senses.title: The act of sending signals
senses.definition: the activity of producing a sign that another party is meant to receive
senses.definitionCN: 制造一个供他方接收的符号的活动
senses.example: Signaling began before any of the animals had moved.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些动物移动之前，信号发送就已经开始。
senses.why: The suffix -ing turns the verb into the name of an ongoing activity, so signaling is the sending seen as a process rather than as a single sign.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ing 把动词变成进行中活动的名称，因此 signaling 是被看作过程的发送，而非单个符号。

senses.title: Biological signal production
senses.titleCN: 生物学意义上的信号产生
senses.definition: the production of a cue by one organism that changes the behavior of another
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物产生线索，从而改变另一生物行为的过程
senses.example: Frog signaling peaks on warm nights after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 蛙类的信号发送在雨后温暖的夜里达到高峰。
senses.why: Biology separates the sender's act from the receiver's response, so signaling names only the first half of the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把发送者的动作与接收者的反应分开，因此 signaling 只命名这次交换的前一半。

senses.title: Telecommunications signaling
senses.definition: the exchange of control information that sets up and manages a connection
senses.definitionCN: 建立与管理连接时交换控制信息的过程
senses.example: The engineers traced the dropped calls to faulty signaling.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把掉话追查到信令故障。
senses.why: A telephone network must agree on how to start and stop a call, and that control conversation is the technical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 电话网络必须就如何开始与结束通话达成一致，这场控制性的对话就是该词的技术义。

senses.title: Cell signaling in biology
senses.definition: the chain by which a cell receives a molecule and passes the message inward
senses.definitionCN: 细胞接收分子并把信息向内部传递的链条
senses.example: The drug blocks signaling at the receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药在受体处阻断信号传导。
senses.why: The same idea of a message sent and received was scaled down to molecules, and the pathway became the standard compound.
senses.whyCN: 「消息被发送与接收」这一想法被缩小到分子层面，通路遂成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Gestural or traffic signaling
senses.definition: the use of visible movements, lights or flags to direct others
senses.definitionCN: 用可见的动作、灯光或旗子指挥他人
senses.example: Night signaling with torches was forbidden on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上禁止用火把做夜间示意。
senses.why: Before wires, the act of sending a visible sign was literal, and that older picture survives in traffic and maritime uses.
senses.whyCN: 在有电线之前，发送可见符号是字面动作，那幅更早的图景仍存于交通与航海用法中。

senses.title: A gesture of intent in business or politics
senses.titleCN: 商业或政治中的示意姿态
senses.definition: an action whose main purpose is to show intention rather than to produce an effect
senses.definitionCN: 主要目的在于表明意图、而非产生实效的动作
senses.example: The small tax cut was signaling, not policy.
senses.exampleCN: 那点减税只是示意，并非政策。
senses.why: When an act is meant to be read rather than used, the act itself becomes a signal, and the activity is called signaling.
senses.whyCN: 当一个动作是为了被解读、而非被使用，动作本身就成了信号，这种活动就叫 signaling。

senses.title: Marking in linguistics
senses.definition: the use of a grammatical or lexical marker to show a category such as politeness or number
senses.definitionCN: 用语法或词汇标记来表明礼貌、数等范畴
senses.example: Polite signaling in that language is carried by verb endings.
senses.exampleCN: 那种语言的礼貌标记由动词词尾承担。
senses.why: A formal feature can carry meaning without being a message, and linguistics borrowed the word for exactly that role.
senses.whyCN: 一个形式特征可以不构成消息却承载意义，语言学正是为这一作用借用该词。

senses.title: Abstract: any display meant to be read
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何供他人解读的展示
senses.definition: any visible or detectable display whose point is to be interpreted by an observer
senses.definitionCN: 任何目的在于被观察者解读的可见或可察觉的展示
senses.example: The empty chair at the table was signaling in its own quiet way.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上那把空椅子以一种安静的方式传递着信号。
senses.why: At its widest, signaling needs no sender with a mind: anything arranged to be read counts.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，signaling 不需要有心的发送者：凡被安排以供解读之物都算。

intro.en: Signaling is signal plus the English gerund suffix -ing. Signal goes back through Old French and Medieval Latin to Latin signum 'mark, sign'. The single l in signaling is American; British writing keeps signalling.
intro.cn: signaling 是 signal 加英语动名词后缀 -ing。signal 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语追溯到拉丁 signum「记号、标志」。signaling 的单 l 拼写属美式，英式写作 signalling。

items.en: Signum meant 'identifying mark, token, military standard, omen'. Its own origin is disputed: one reconstruction connects it with a root meaning 'to follow', another with a root meaning 'to cut', and the matter is not settled.
items.cn: signum 意为「识别记号、凭信、军旗、征兆」。其自身来源有争议：一种重构把它联系到意为「跟随」的词根，另一种联系到意为「切割」的词根，至今未定。

items.en: Late Latin signalis 'used as a sign' supplied Medieval Latin signale 'a signal', the immediate source of the French and English words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 signalis「用作记号的」给出中世纪拉丁 signale「信号」，后者是法语与英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French signal 'seal, imprint, sign, mark' entered English in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 signal「印记、标志、记号」在 14 世纪晚期进入英语。

items.en: The noun is recorded from the late fourteenth century; the restricted sense 'an agreed sign to act' is from the 1590s.
items.cn: 该名词自 14 世纪晚期有记录；「约定俗成、据以行动的信号」这一收窄义自 16 世纪 90 年代出现。

items.en: The suffix -ing comes from Old English -ung and names an action or its result, as in building and warning.
items.cn: 后缀 -ing 来自古英语 -ung，命名动作或其结果，如 building 与 warning。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): signum's pre-Latin history has competing reconstructions, and the earliest use of signaling as a standalone noun is not fixed, so the date should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：signum 在拉丁语之前的历史存在彼此竞争的重构；signaling 作为独立名词的最早用法也无定论，因此年代应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the base word, the British spelling and inflected forms that differ only in grammar; group two holds nouns that name other parts of the same exchange.
note.cn: 第一组区分词基、英式拼写与仅语法不同的屈折形式；第二组是命名同一次交换中其他部分的名词。

entries.definition: The British form with double l; identical in meaning, different only in orthography.
entries.definitionCN: 双 l 的英式形式；意义相同，仅在正字法上不同。

entries.definition: The noun and verb from which signaling is formed; it names a sign or the act of sending one.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 signaling 的名词与动词；命名符号或发送符号的动作。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb; it reports a completed act and cannot stand as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式；报告已完成的动作，不能充当名词。

entries.definition: From signum via Old French: a small seal, an object that makes a mark rather than an act of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 signum：小印章，是留下记号的物件，而非发送动作。

entries.definition: The whole two-way process of sharing meaning; signaling is only the sender's side.
entries.definitionCN: 共享意义的整个双向过程；signaling 只是发送者一侧。

entries.definition: Giving a prompt that triggers a response; it stresses the trigger rather than the message.
entries.definitionCN: 给出触发反应的提示；强调触发，而非消息。

entries.definition: The carrying of a signal through a medium; it says nothing about a receiver interpreting it.
entries.definitionCN: 信号通过介质传输；不涉及接收者是否解读。

entries.definition: Making visible bodily movements to convey something; one channel of signaling.
entries.definitionCN: 做出可见的身体动作来传达；是 signaling 的一个渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: signal + -ing: the act of sending a sign.
normal.cn: signal + -ing：发送符号的动作。

normal.en: The family runs signal, signaling, signaler, signalize, signalling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 signal、signaling、signaler、signalize、signalling。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: signaling pathway, cell signaling, signaling system, honest signaling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：信号传导通路、细胞信号传导、信令系统、诚实信号。

normal.en: British writing doubles the l: signalling.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l：signalling。

normal.en: The root signum also gives sign, signal, signature and signet.
normal.cn: 词根 signum 还给出 sign、signal、signature 与 signet。

abstract.en: Picture a frog's call travelling outward as rings on dark water.
abstract.cn: 想象蛙鸣像黑水面上的同心圆向外扩散。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair arranged carefully so that everyone reads it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被刻意摆好的空椅子，让所有人都读出意思。

abstract.en: Picture a cell answering a molecule the way a room answers a knock.
abstract.cn: 想象细胞回应一个分子，就像房间回应一次敲门。

examples.en: Chemical signaling between roots and soil microbes is under intense study.
examples.cn: 根系与土壤微生物之间的化学信号传递正被密集研究。

examples.en: Faulty signaling, not the cable, caused the outage.
examples.cn: 造成中断的是信令故障，而非电缆。

examples.en: The peacock's display is signaling aimed at a single watching female.
examples.cn: 孔雀的展示是针对唯一一位观看的雌性的信号发送。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「signal（信号）+ ing（正在进行）」——正在把信号发出去的过程 → 信号发送、信令

root: signal（拉丁 signum「记号」经中世纪拉丁 signale、古法语 signal）+ -ing（古英语 -ung，表动作）；美式单 l，英式双 l；signum 更深来源有两种竞争性重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act outward: a sign is made, then made by an animal, then by a network, then by a cell, then by a hand, then by an institution, then by a grammar, and finally by anything arranged to be read.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个向外发出的动作：先造出符号，再由动物、网络、细胞、手势、机构、语法，最后由任何被安排以供解读之物造出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign leaving a sender and travelling until someone reads it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个符号离开发送者，一路行进，直到有人读出它。

branches.en: SENDER'S SIDE: the general act, then the biological half that excludes the receiver's response.
branches.cn: 发送者一侧：一般动作，以及排除接收者反应的生物学那一半。

branches.en: SCALED SYSTEMS: telephone control signals and molecular pathways use the same shape.
branches.cn: 不同尺度的系统：电话控制信号与分子通路共享同一形状。

branches.en: VISIBLE ORDER: lights and flags direct bodies in space.
branches.cn: 可见的秩序：灯光与旗子在空间中指挥身体。

branches.en: MADE TO BE INTERPRETED: political gestures and grammatical markers both ask to be read.
branches.cn: 为被解读而造：政治姿态与语法标记都要求被读出。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any display arranged for an observer.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何为观察者安排好的展示。

intro.en: Signaling is a Latin-derived noun plus a native English suffix, a common hybrid pattern in technical vocabulary.
intro.cn: signaling 是拉丁来源名词加本族英语后缀，是术语中常见的混合模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'mark' gives sign, signal, signature and signet; the suffix -ing is native English, from Old English -ung.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 signum「记号」给出 sign、signal、signature 与 signet；后缀 -ing 属本族英语，来自古英语 -ung。

items.example: The root underlies sign and signal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是 sign 与 signal 的基础。

items.example: The lighthouse sends a signal every twelve seconds.
items.exampleCN: 灯塔每十二秒发出一次信号。

items.example: Building, warning and signaling all name activities.
items.exampleCN: building、warning 与 signaling 都命名活动。

items.example: Signaling precedes any response.
items.exampleCN: 信号发送先于任何回应。

items.example: British manuals print signalling.
items.exampleCN: 英国手册写作 signalling。

items.example: The signaler stood where the ships could see.
items.exampleCN: 发信号的人站在船只能看见的地方。

items.example: The victory was signalized by a bell.
items.exampleCN: 这场胜利以钟声表明。

items.example: A sign can stand without being sent.
items.exampleCN: 符号可以不经过发送而存在。

items.example: The signature is a sign made by hand.
items.exampleCN: 签名是用手做出的符号。

definition_zh: 信号；暗号；示意动作；发信号；表明；显著的（书面）
definition_en: a sign or event that conveys information or instructions, or to send such a sign
core_image: 灯塔每隔十二秒闪一次，船员不必听见任何声音，就知道自己离岸还有多远
scene: 灯塔每十二秒闪一次，船员不用听任何声音就能确定自己离岸还有多远。 The lighthouse flashes once every twelve seconds, and the crew can fix their distance from shore without a word: a signal that needs no language.
sceneCN: 这里 signal 指「承载信息的可见符号」（第 1 个义项：信号、暗号）；句意为灯塔按固定间隔闪光，船员据此判断离岸距离，是一种无需语言的信号。可辨识物件：灯塔、旋转灯罩、海面、船甲板。

pos.zh: 显著的；值得注意的（书面，较旧）

collocations.zh: 混乱的信号；含糊的示意

senses.title: A sign conveying information
senses.titleCN: 承载信息的信号或暗号
senses.definition: a sound, movement, light or mark that is understood to carry a message
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为承载消息的声音、动作、光或记号
senses.example: Three short blasts were the agreed signal to retreat.
senses.exampleCN: 三声短鸣是约定的撤退信号。
senses.why: Latin signum is an identifying mark, and a signal is that mark made at a distance so that someone else can act on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 signum 是识别记号，而信号就是把这个记号放到远处，让他人据以行动。

senses.title: A gesture of instruction
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or body used to tell someone what to do
senses.definitionCN: 用手或身体的动作告诉某人该怎么做
senses.example: The officer gave the signal and the line moved forward.
senses.exampleCN: 军官一示意，队列就向前移动。
senses.why: The body can be the medium as well as the light: any movement can serve as the mark, provided both sides know its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能充当媒介，正如灯光一样：只要双方知道含义，任何动作都能充当记号。

senses.title: An electronic or radio signal
senses.definition: a varying current or wave that carries information through a device
senses.definitionCN: 通过设备承载信息的变动电流或波
senses.example: The storm reduced the signal to static.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨把信号削弱成一片杂音。
senses.why: Telegraphy turned the visible mark into a modulation of current, and the old noun was transferred to the invisible wave.
senses.whyCN: 电报把可见记号变成电流的调制，旧名词于是转移到看不见的波上。

senses.title: A traffic signal
senses.definition: a set of lights that orders vehicles and pedestrians to stop or go
senses.definitionCN: 指挥车辆与行人停或走的一组灯
senses.example: The signal turned green and the queue dissolved.
senses.exampleCN: 信号灯转绿，队伍随即散开。
senses.why: Where many must obey one mark at once, the mark becomes an object in the street, and the noun names that object.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人必须同时服从同一个记号，记号就成了街上的物件，名词便命名该物件。

senses.title: An indication of a coming event
senses.titleCN: 预示某事将发生的迹象
senses.definition: an observable fact that suggests what is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 暗示即将发生什么的可观察事实
senses.example: Falling orders are a signal of weaker demand.
senses.exampleCN: 订单下滑是需求走弱的信号。
senses.why: Because anyone can read an event as a mark of another event, the word extends from deliberate signs to natural ones.
senses.whyCN: 因为任何人都能把一个事件读作另一事件的记号，这个词就从有意符号扩展到自然迹象。

senses.title: To send a sign
senses.definition: to make a sound, movement or light in order to convey an instruction or intention
senses.definitionCN: 发出声音、动作或光，以传达指示或意图
senses.example: The driver signaled left well before the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在转弯前很早就打了左转信号。
senses.why: The verb, recorded from 1805, simply reverses the noun: to be the one who makes the mark rather than the one who reads it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词自 1805 年有记录，只是把名词反过来：做记号的人，而非读记号的人。

senses.title: To indicate or point to
senses.definition: to show or suggest something indirectly through an action or fact
senses.definitionCN: 通过动作或事实间接显示、暗示某事
senses.example: The handshake signaled a new stage in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次握手标志着会谈进入新阶段。
senses.why: If an act can stand for an intention, then performing the act is a way of announcing the intention without naming it.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个动作能代表某种意图，那么做出该动作，就是在不点名的情况下宣告该意图。

senses.title: Adjective: notably exceptional
senses.titleCN: 形容词：显著的、出众的（较旧用法）
senses.definition: striking, remarkable, notably worth attention, a usage now mostly literary
senses.definitionCN: 突出的、值得注意的，今多用于书面文学
senses.example: The rescue was a signal act of courage.
senses.exampleCN: 那次救援是一次非凡的勇敢之举。
senses.why: From the notion of a mark that stands out, the word became an adjective for anything that deserves to be pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 从「突出的记号」这一想法出发，这个词成了形容词，指任何值得被指出的东西。

intro.en: Signal comes through Old French and Medieval Latin from Latin signum 'mark, sign'. The noun enters English in the late fourteenth century, the verb in 1805, and the electrical sense dates from the 1850s.
intro.cn: signal 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语来自拉丁 signum「记号、标志」。名词在 14 世纪晚期进入英语，动词在 1805 年出现，电学义可追溯到 19 世纪 50 年代。

items.en: Signum covered 'identifying mark, token, military standard, omen, constellation'. Two competing reconstructions exist for its own origin, one from a root 'to follow' and one from a root 'to cut', and neither has won.
items.cn: signum 涵盖「识别记号、凭信、军旗、征兆、星座」。其自身来源有两种竞争性重构，一种出自意为「跟随」的词根，一种出自意为「切割」的词根，均未胜出。

items.en: Signalis 'used as a sign' produced Medieval Latin signale 'a signal', the bridge to French.
items.cn: signalis「用作记号的」产生中世纪拉丁 signale「信号」，成为通往法语的桥梁。

items.en: Old French signal meant 'seal, imprint, sign, mark', and entered English in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 signal 意为「印记、标志、记号」，于 14 世纪晚期进入英语。

items.en: From the 1590s the noun named a conventional sign agreed on to start or stop something, which is the core of the modern meaning.
items.cn: 自 16 世纪 90 年代起，该名词指约定俗成、用于开始或停止某事的符号，这是现代词义的核心。

items.en: By 1855 signal named the modulation of an electric current, and the word later moved to radio waves and broadcasting.
items.cn: 到 1855 年，signal 指电流的调制，后来这个词又移用于无线电波与广播。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the two reconstructions for signum remain undecided, and the adjective 'remarkable' is an irregular adoption from French signalé, so its date and formation are both approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：signum 的两种重构仍无定论；形容词「显著的」义是从法语 signalé 不规则借入，其年代与构成都只能视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates words from the same signum stock that differ in grammar or meaning; group two holds cues and indications that are not deliberately sent.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出 signum 词干、在语法或意义上不同的词；第二组是并非有意发送的线索与迹象。

entries.definition: From the same signum: any mark or indication, whether or not anyone sends it; a signal is a sign made to be received.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 signum：任何记号或迹象，不论是否有人发送；signal 是为被接收而做出的 sign。

entries.definition: From signare 'to mark': a person's own written mark, an identity sign rather than a message.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 signare「标记」：个人书写的记号，是身份符号而非消息。

entries.definition: The gerund naming the activity of sending signals, as against the sign itself.
entries.definitionCN: 动名词，命名发送信号的活动，与符号本身相对。

entries.definition: From significare 'to make known': it means important, not a sign that is sent.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 significare「使知晓」：意为重要，而非被发送的符号。

entries.definition: A prompt that tells someone when to act; it is often smaller and more situational than a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 告诉人何时行动的提示；常比 signal 更小、更依赖情境。

entries.definition: A piece of evidence that something is true or coming; nobody needs to have sent it.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物为真或即将发生的证据；不需要有人发送它。

entries.definition: A movement of the body that expresses meaning; it is one physical channel a signal can use.
entries.definitionCN: 表达意义的身体动作；是信号可使用的一种身体渠道。

entries.definition: A light or other device set in place to guide or warn; it is a source of signals rather than the message.
entries.definitionCN: 为引导或警示而安置的灯或装置；是信号的来源，而非消息本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: signum 'mark' + -al: a mark made so that someone can act on it.
normal.cn: signum「记号」+ -al：为了让别人据以行动而做出的记号。

normal.en: The family runs sign, signal, signaling, signaler, signature, significant.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sign、signal、signaling、signaler、signature、significant。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: send a signal, traffic signal, signal strength, mixed signals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：发出信号、交通信号灯、信号强度、混乱的信号。

normal.en: The verb is 1805, the electric sense 1855: the word keeps moving with technology.
normal.cn: 动词出现于 1805 年，电学义在 1855 年：这个词不断随技术迁移。

normal.en: American spelling doubles nothing: signaled, signaling; British doubles the l.
normal.cn: 美式不双写：signaled、signaling；英式双写 l。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that says the same word every twelve seconds and is never wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏每十二秒说同一个词、从不出错的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a crowd that stops a whole line without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象人群中举起的一只手，无声地让整条队伍停下。

abstract.en: Picture a falling number that tells a whole industry what is coming.
abstract.cn: 想象一个下滑的数字，向整个行业预告将要发生什么。

examples.en: The referee's signal stopped play before anyone was hurt.
examples.cn: 裁判的示意在有人受伤之前就中止了比赛。

examples.en: A sudden silence in the gallery signaled that the painting had sold.
examples.cn: 画廊里突然的安静表明那幅画已经售出。

examples.en: The signal was too weak to reach the valley.
examples.cn: 信号太弱，传不到山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sign（记号）+ al（名词）」——做出来给人看的记号 → 信号、暗号、示意

root: 拉丁 signum「记号、标志」→ 中世纪拉丁 signale「信号」→ 古法语 signal → 英语 signal；signum 自身来源有「跟随」与「切割」两种重构，尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one mark from a distant lamp to a hand, a wire, a street light, a market statistic, an act of sending, an indirect announcement, and finally anything that stands out.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个记号：从远处的灯，到手势、电线、街灯、市场统计、发送动作、间接宣告，最后到任何突出之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark repeated at a distance so that another can act on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在远处重复出现的记号，供他人据以行动。

branches.en: MADE TO BE READ: a mark at a distance, or a movement close at hand.
branches.cn: 为被读出而做：或远处记号，或近处动作。

branches.en: CARRIED BY TECHNOLOGY: the same mark becomes a wave, then an object in the street.
branches.cn: 由技术承载：同一记号先变成波，再变成街上的物件。

branches.en: READ WITHOUT A SENDER: a natural fact treated as a mark of what comes next.
branches.cn: 无需发送者也能读：自然事实被当作下一件事的记号。

branches.en: THE VERB TURNS THE NOUN AROUND: to make the mark, or to announce by making it.
branches.cn: 动词把名词反过来：做出记号，或通过做记号来宣告。

branches.en: THE MARK THAT STANDS OUT: anything worth pointing at.
branches.cn: 突出的记号：任何值得被指出的东西。

intro.en: Signal is a Latin root with a Latin adjective suffix and a native verb ending; the family is unusually large because the root also gives sign and signature.
intro.cn: signal 是拉丁词根加拉丁形容词后缀，再加本族动词词尾；由于该词根还给出 sign 与 signature，这个词族异常庞大。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'mark' gives sign, signal, signature and signet; Late Latin signalis 'used as a sign' gives the adjective form that French and English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 signum「记号」给出 sign、signal、signature 与 signet；晚期拉丁 signalis「用作记号的」给出法语与英语借用的形容词形式。

items.example: The root is visible in sign and signal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在 sign 与 signal 中可见。

items.example: Signalis meant 'of a sign'.
items.exampleCN: signalis 意为「属于记号的」。

items.example: The signal came at noon.
items.exampleCN: 信号在正午传来。

items.example: The tower signals every hour.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔每小时发一次信号。

items.example: She signaled with both hands.
items.exampleCN: 她双手示意。

items.example: Signaling stopped when the storm began.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨开始时信号发送中断了。

items.example: The signaler raised a red flag.
items.exampleCN: 发信号的人举起红旗。

items.example: A sign need not be sent.
items.exampleCN: 记号不必被发送。

items.example: The signature closed the letter.
items.exampleCN: 签名结束了这封信。

items.example: The drop was significant.
items.exampleCN: 这一下降很显著。

definition_zh: 求爱；追求；求偶期；（动物）求偶行为
definition_en: the period and the behavior through which one person or animal tries to win the affection and consent of another
core_image: 雄孔雀把巨大的尾屏完全展开，绕雌鸟缓慢转身，每一个姿势都停同样一拍
scene: 雄孔雀把尾屏完全展开，绕雌鸟缓慢转身，每个姿势都保持同样一拍。 The male peacock fans his tail and turns slowly around the female, holding each position for the same beat: a courtship that follows a fixed script.
sceneCN: 这里 courtship 指「为赢得对方好感而进行的一整套展示行为」（第 3 个义项：动物求偶行为）；句意为雄孔雀按固定节奏展开尾屏、绕雌鸟转身，这正是求偶。可辨识物件：展开的尾屏、雌鸟、草地、固定停留的姿势。

pos.zh: （动物行为学）求偶行为；求偶展示

forms.label: 复数（多段追求期；多种求偶行为）
相关名词（宫廷；球场；追求）

derivatives.zh: 有礼的（同出 court，语义已偏）

senses.title: The act of wooing a person
senses.titleCN: 追求某人、争取其好感的行为
senses.definition: the attention and effort one person gives another in order to win affection
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为赢得另一人好感而付出的关注与努力
senses.example: Their courtship lasted two years before the engagement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的追求持续了两年才订婚。
senses.why: The word began as the behaviour of a courtier, someone who attends a court, and the polite attention of that role became the model for winning favour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指朝臣的举止，即在宫廷中侍奉的人所表现的那种礼数，而这份周到的关注后来成了赢得欢心的范本。

senses.title: The period before a union
senses.definition: the stretch of time during which two people develop a romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 两个人发展恋爱关系所经历的一段时间
senses.example: The novel describes a long rural courtship of letters and walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了一段由书信与散步构成的漫长乡间追求期。
senses.why: Because wooing takes time, the noun came to name the time itself, not only the acts within it.
senses.whyCN: 因为追求需要时间，这个名词便开始命名那段时间，而不只是其中的动作。

senses.title: Animal courtship behavior
senses.definition: the displays and signals by which an animal solicits a mate
senses.definitionCN: 动物为招引配偶而进行的展示与信号
senses.example: The dance is courtship, and the female chooses on the basis of it.
senses.exampleCN: 这场舞就是求偶，雌性据此做出选择。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the human word for the same sequence of approach, display and acceptance, because the shape of the behaviour is recognisably alike.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个人类词，用来指同样由接近、展示与接受构成的序列，因为行为形状明显相似。

senses.title: A fixed sequence of displays
senses.definition: a stereotyped order of movements performed in a set order before mating
senses.definitionCN: 交配前按固定顺序进行的一套刻板动作
senses.example: The courtship has eleven steps, and a missed step ends it.
senses.exampleCN: 这套求偶有十一个步骤，漏掉一步就结束。
senses.why: Once courtship is a signal, it can be scripted, and a script that must be followed exactly is what makes the display readable to a partner.
senses.whyCN: 一旦求偶成为信号，它就可以被写成脚本；而必须严格遵循的脚本，正是让展示对配偶可读的原因。

senses.title: Gifts and feeding as courtship
senses.titleCN: 以礼物或喂食作为求偶
senses.definition: the offering of food or objects as part of wooing
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或物件作为追求的一部分献上
senses.example: In some species courtship means a gift of prey.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些物种里，求偶意味着一份猎物作礼物。
senses.why: A gift is a display that costs the giver something, and cost is exactly what makes it evidence of serious intent.
senses.whyCN: 礼物是让给出者付出代价的展示，而代价正是使它成为认真意图之证据的东西。

senses.title: The art of paying court
senses.definition: attentive behaviour aimed at winning the favour of someone powerful
senses.definitionCN: 为赢得有权者青睐而表现出的殷勤举止
senses.example: His courtship of the committee was tireless and transparent.
senses.exampleCN: 他对委员会的争取不知疲倦，也毫不掩饰。
senses.why: The courtier's original task was to gain favour, and that older political sense survives whenever someone courts a body rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 朝臣原本的任务就是争取恩宠，只要有人追求的是一个机构而非一个人，这个更早的政治义就会复活。

senses.title: A campaign to win support
senses.definition: a sustained effort to attract voters, clients or allies
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引选民、客户或盟友而进行的持续努力
senses.example: The party's courtship of rural voters began early.
senses.exampleCN: 该党对乡村选民的争取很早就开始了。
senses.why: Political language borrows the whole arc of wooing, from first approach to promised union, and applies it to blocs of supporters.
senses.whyCN: 政治语言借用了求爱的整条弧线，从初次接近到许诺结合，并把它用于支持者群体。

senses.title: Abstract: the art of winning over
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：赢得人心的技艺
senses.definition: any deliberate effort to turn indifference into acceptance
senses.definitionCN: 任何把冷淡转为接纳的有意努力
senses.example: The book is a courtship of the reader, patient and unhurried.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对读者的一次追求，耐心而不催促。
senses.why: At its widest the word describes a strategy of approach rather than a relationship, and that is why it can be applied to readers or ideas.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词描述一种接近的策略，而非一段关系，因此它能用于读者或观念。

intro.en: Courtship is court plus the native suffix -ship. Court comes through Old French from Latin cohors 'enclosed yard, company of attendants', and -ship from Old English -scipe 'state or condition of being'.
intro.cn: courtship 是 court 加本族后缀 -ship。court 经古法语来自拉丁 cohors「围起的院子、随从队伍」，-ship 来自古英语 -scipe「处于某种状态」。

items.en: Cohors meant 'enclosed yard, enclosure', and also 'a company of soldiers or attendants'. The link to hortus 'garden' is generally accepted, both going back to a root meaning 'to enclose'.
items.cn: cohors 意为「围起的院子、围场」，也指「一队士兵或随从」。它与 hortus「花园」的联系一般被接受，两者都可追溯到意为「围住」的词根。

items.en: Old French cort 'king's court, princely residence' entered English in the late twelfth century, bringing both the place and the assembled company.
items.cn: 古法语 cort「国王的宫廷、君主居所」在 12 世纪晚期进入英语，同时带来地点与聚集的人群两层意思。

items.en: Old English -scipe formed abstract nouns of state or condition, as in friendship and lordship; it gives courtship the sense of a role or a period.
items.cn: 古英语 -scipe 构成表示状态或身份的名词，如 friendship 与 lordship；它使 courtship 带有「角色或时期」的意思。

items.en: Courtship is recorded from the 1570s meaning 'the behaviour of a courtier, the arts of a court'.
items.cn: courtship 自 16 世纪 70 年代有记录，义为「朝臣的举止、宫廷的技艺」。

items.en: By the 1590s the word named the attention paid to win someone's affection, and by the 1830s it named the whole period of a developing romance.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 90 年代，这个词指为赢得某人好感而付出的关注；到 19 世纪 30 年代，它指整段发展中的恋情。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the animal sense): the biological use of courtship is twentieth-century usage, and no single earliest citation is agreed, so it should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（动物义的首见年代）：courtship 的生物学用法属 20 世纪，最早书证没有统一说法，因此应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates words from the same court stock that now mean different things; group two holds nouns for neighbouring stages of the same approach.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出 court 词干、今义不同的词；第二组是同一接近过程中相邻阶段的名词。

entries.definition: The source noun: a royal court, a playing area, or the verb 'to woo'; courtship is the abstract noun of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 来源名词：宫廷、球场，或动词「追求」；courtship 是该动词的抽象名词。

entries.definition: From the manners expected at court: it means polite, with no reference to wooing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自宫廷应有的礼数：意为有礼，与求爱无关。

entries.definition: A person who attends a royal court; the original courtship was this person's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 出入宫廷的人；最初的 courtship 正是这种人的举止。

entries.definition: Polite behaviour as a social code; it shares the court root but not the romantic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 作为社交规范的礼貌举止；共用 court 词根，但无恋爱义。

entries.definition: The activity of trying to win someone's love; it stresses effort, while courtship can also name the period.
entries.definitionCN: 争取某人爱的活动；强调努力，而 courtship 也可指那段时间。

entries.definition: A show put on to be seen; in biology a courtship display is one part of courtship.
entries.definitionCN: 为被看见而做的展示；在生物学中，求偶展示是求偶的一部分。

entries.definition: Playful romantic attention without a promise of union; courtship implies a serious aim.
entries.definitionCN: 不带结合承诺的轻佻浪漫关注；courtship 含有认真目标。

entries.definition: The act or period of pairing for reproduction; it follows courtship and is not the same as it.
entries.definitionCN: 为繁殖而配对的行为或时期；位于求偶之后，并不等同于求偶。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: court + -ship: the state or art of paying court.
normal.cn: court + -ship：处于「奉承、争取」之中的状态或技艺。

normal.en: The family runs court, courtship, courteous, courtier, courtesy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 court、courtship、courteous、courtier、courtesy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: courtship display, courtship behavior, during courtship, courtship rituals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：求偶展示、求偶行为、在求偶期间、求偶仪式。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the behaviour of a courtier, not of a lover.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是在朝臣的举止，而非恋人的举止。

normal.en: Courtship precedes mating; the two words name different stages.
normal.cn: 求偶先于交配；两个词命名不同阶段。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of feathers opened like a letter written only to one reader.
abstract.cn: 想象一把羽毛扇展开，像一封只写给一个读者的信。

abstract.en: Picture a gift that costs the giver enough to prove the intention.
abstract.cn: 想象一份让给出者付出足够代价、从而证明意图的礼物。

abstract.en: Picture a book that slowly turns a stranger into a companion.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书慢慢把陌生人变成同伴。

examples.en: Their courtship began with letters and ended with a shared house.
examples.cn: 他们的追求始于书信，终于同住一个屋檐。

examples.en: The male's courtship includes a gift of a small fish.
examples.cn: 雄性的求偶包括献上一条小鱼。

examples.en: The committee responded to months of quiet courtship.
examples.cn: 委员会对数月来低调的争取作出了回应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「court（宫廷/追求）+ ship（状态）」——像朝臣一样殷勤地争取对方好感 → 求爱、求偶

root: court（拉丁 cohors「围场、随从队伍」经古法语 cort）+ -ship（古英语 -scipe，表状态）；由「朝臣举止」引申为「求爱、求偶」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one approach: attention paid to win favour, then the time it takes, then the animal version, the scripted display, the gift, the political flattery, the campaign, and finally any art of winning over.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个接近动作：先是为赢得青睐付出的关注，再是所花的时间、动物版本、脚本化展示、礼物、政治奉承、争取活动，最后是任何赢得人心的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a careful, repeated approach made to turn indifference into acceptance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次周到而反复的接近，把冷淡转为接纳。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DURATION: attention given, and the time that attention fills.
branches.cn: 动作与时长：付出的关注，以及这份关注填满的时间。

branches.en: BORROWED BY BIOLOGY: the human shape becomes a display with a fixed order.
branches.cn: 被生物学借用：人类的形状变成有固定次序的展示。

branches.en: COSTLY PROOF: a gift shows that the intention is not idle.
branches.cn: 昂贵的证明：礼物表明意图并非空话。

branches.en: FROM PERSON TO BODY: flattering a patron, then courting a bloc of voters.
branches.cn: 从人到机构：先奉承恩主，再争取一群选民。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: any strategy for winning someone over.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何赢得他人接纳的策略。

intro.en: Courtship is a Latin-derived noun with a native Germanic suffix; both halves are productive, and the court family is large.
intro.cn: courtship 是拉丁来源名词加本族日耳曼后缀；两半都有构词力，court 词族也很大。

latinIntro.en: Latin cohors 'enclosed yard, retinue' gives court and its family, including courteous and courtier; the suffix -ship is not Latin but Old English -scipe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cohors「围场、随从」给出 court 及其词族，包括 courteous 与 courtier；后缀 -ship 并非拉丁语，而是古英语 -scipe。

items.structure: cohors / cortem (Latin) via Old French cort
items.example: The word first named a place and its people.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初命名一个地点及其人群。

items.example: Friendship and lordship use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: friendship 与 lordship 使用同一后缀。

items.meaning: the state or art of paying court
items.meaningCN: 奉承、追求的状态或技艺
items.example: Their courtship was long.
items.exampleCN: 他们的追求期很长。

items.example: The study compares courtships across species.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究比较不同物种的求偶行为。

items.example: A courtier's poise became the model for wooing.
items.exampleCN: 朝臣的仪态成了追求的范本。

items.example: The reply was courteous but firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个答复有礼而坚定。

items.example: Courtesy costs nothing.
items.exampleCN: 礼貌不费分文。

items.example: Courtship-related plumage is often the brightest.
items.exampleCN: 与求偶有关的羽色往往最亮。

items.example: The suitor waited at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 追求者在门外等候。

definition_zh: 交配；配对；（作定语）交配的；交配期的
definition_en: the act or period of pairing of animals for reproduction, or the forming of a matched pair
core_image: 两只蜻蜓在水面上方连成一个轮状，贴着水面一起滑行几秒便分开
scene: 两只蜻蜓在水面上方连成一个轮状，贴着水面一起滑行片刻便分开。 Two dragonflies lock into a wheel above the pond and glide across the surface together, a mating that lasts only a few minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 mating 指「动物为繁殖而配对的行为」（第 1 个义项：交配行为）；句意为两只蜻蜓连成轮状、贴水滑行片刻便分开，整个过程只持续几分钟。可辨识物件：连成轮的蜻蜓、水面、芦苇、短暂的时间。

pos.zh: 交配的；交配期的（作定语）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多个配对事件）

senses.title: The act of pairing for reproduction
senses.definition: the act by which two animals come together to reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 两只动物为繁殖而结合的行为
senses.example: Mating takes place once the female accepts the display.
senses.exampleCN: 雌性接受展示之后才会发生交配。
senses.why: The noun mate named a companion or spouse, and the gerund mating names the act of coming together as a pair.
senses.whyCN: 名词 mate 命名同伴或配偶，动名词 mating 则命名作为一对结合起来的动作。

senses.title: The period of pairing
senses.definition: the season or stretch of time in which animals pair
senses.definitionCN: 动物配对的季节或一段时间
senses.example: Mating begins with the first warm rain.
senses.exampleCN: 交配随第一场暖雨开始。
senses.why: A gerund can name a time as well as an act, especially when the event is seasonal and predictable.
senses.whyCN: 动名词既能命名动作，也能命名时间，尤其当事件随季节发生且可预测时。

senses.title: The mating system of a species
senses.definition: the pattern a species follows in choosing and keeping partners, such as monogamy or polygyny
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种在选择与维持配偶上的模式，如一雄一雌或多雌
senses.example: The species has a mating system built on short pair bonds.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种的交配制度建立在短暂的配偶关系上。
senses.why: If pairing follows a pattern, the pattern can be named, and 'mating system' became the standard term for it.
senses.whyCN: 如果配对遵循某种模式，模式就能被命名，「交配制度」遂成为它的标准说法。

senses.title: A mating strategy
senses.definition: one of the alternative tactics an animal uses to obtain mates
senses.definitionCN: 动物为获得配偶而采用的替代策略之一
senses.example: Small males adopt a mating strategy that avoids the main arena.
senses.exampleCN: 体型小的雄性采取一种避开主战场的交配策略。
senses.why: Where partners are scarce, pairing becomes a problem with alternatives, and each alternative is called a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 当配偶稀缺时，配对就成了有替代方案的问题，每个方案便被称为一种策略。

senses.title: Breeding and cross-breeding
senses.definition: the controlled pairing of plants or animals by breeders
senses.definitionCN: 育种者有控制地把植物或动物配对
senses.example: The mating of the two lines produced a hardier grain.
senses.exampleCN: 两个品系的配种产生了更耐逆的谷物。
senses.why: Human breeders took the word from animal pairing and applied it to any controlled union of varieties.
senses.whyCN: 人类育种者从动物配对借来这个词，用于任何有控制的品种结合。

senses.title: Technical pairing of parts
senses.definition: the joining of two matching parts or devices into one assembly
senses.definitionCN: 把两个相配的零件或装置接成一个组件
senses.example: Check the mating of the connector before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 测试前检查接头的配合。
senses.why: The image of two things made to fit is old, and engineering reuses it for parts that must join exactly.
senses.whyCN: 两物被做成相合的形状，这个意象很古老，工程学把它复用于必须精确接合的零件。

senses.title: A temporary pair bond
senses.definition: the short association formed for one breeding attempt
senses.definitionCN: 为一次繁殖尝试而形成的短暂联结
senses.example: Their mating lasts a day; the eggs are left alone.
senses.exampleCN: 它们的配对只持续一天，卵被独自留下。
senses.why: Because mating is an event, it can also name the brief union that the event creates.
senses.whyCN: 因为交配是一个事件，它也能命名该事件造成的短暂结合。

senses.title: Abstract: any matched joining
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何成对的结合
senses.definition: any joining of two things that are made for each other
senses.definitionCN: 任何两个彼此相配之物的结合
senses.example: The mating of old brick and new glass defines the building.
senses.exampleCN: 旧砖与新玻璃的结合定义了这座建筑。
senses.why: At its widest, the word needs no animals: two things that fit together can be said to mate.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词不需要动物：两个彼此相合的东西也能被说成「结合」。

intro.en: Mating is the gerund of the verb mate, which came from the noun mate 'companion, spouse'. The noun is from Middle Low German mate, gemate 'one eating at the same table'.
intro.cn: mating 是动词 mate 的动名词，而 mate 来自名词 mate「同伴、配偶」。该名词来自中低地德语 mate、gemate「同桌吃饭的人」。

items.en: The compound meant '(one) having food together', from *ga- 'together' plus *matiz 'food'; the same *matiz gives English meat.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「共同有食物的人」，由 *ga-「共同」加 *matiz「食物」构成；同一个 *matiz 也给出英语 meat。

items.en: Middle Low German mate, gemate 'messmate, companion' entered English in the mid-fourteenth century as 'associate, fellow'.
items.cn: 中低地德语 mate、gemate「同餐伙伴、同伴」在 14 世纪中叶进入英语，义为「伙伴、同伴」。

items.en: By the 1540s mate named one of a married pair, and the animal sense of a partner followed from that.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 40 年代，mate 指已婚一对中的一方，动物配偶义由此引申。

items.en: The verb mate is recorded from about 1500 meaning 'to match or couple', and the animal sense 'to pair for breeding' from about 1600.
items.cn: 动词 mate 自约 1500 年有记录，意为「配对、结合」，其「为繁殖而配对」的动物义约自 1600 年出现。

items.en: Mating is the ordinary -ing form of that verb, and it became the standard biological noun in the twentieth century.
items.cn: mating 是该动词普通的 -ing 形式，到 20 世纪成为标准的生物学名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the reconstruction of *matiz and its Indo-European connections is debated, and the earliest citation of mating as a technical term is not fixed, so both should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*matiz 的重构及其印欧语联系存有争论；mating 作为术语的最早书证也无定论，因此两者都应视为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the verb, the person noun and a look-alike from the chess word; group two holds terms for the stages around mating.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词、表人名词与来自国际象棋的形近词；第二组是与交配相邻阶段的术语。

entries.definition: The noun and verb behind mating: a companion, a spouse, or to pair.
entries.definitionCN: mating 背后的名词与动词：同伴、配偶，或配对。

entries.definition: The past participle, used as an adjective for animals that have already paired.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，作形容词指已经配对的动物。

entries.definition: British informal for friendly, from mate 'companion'; it has nothing to do with breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「友好的」，来自 mate「同伴」；与繁殖无关。

entries.definition: From Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless', through Old French: it is not related to mate 'companion'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」，经古法语；与 mate「同伴」无关。

entries.definition: The whole process of producing offspring, including nesting and care; mating is one step in it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生后代的整个过程，包括筑巢与照料；mating 只是其中一步。

entries.definition: The forming of a pair, which may or may not involve reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形成一对，可能涉及繁殖，也可能不涉及。

entries.definition: The physical act of sexual union; mating also covers the whole pairing period and system.
entries.definitionCN: 性结合的身体动作；mating 还涵盖整个配对期与制度。

entries.definition: The displays that come before mating and often decide whether it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 交配之前的展示，常决定交配是否发生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.cn: mate + -ing：配对的动名词，来自动词。

normal.en: The family runs mate, mating, mated, matey, pairing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mate、mating、mated、matey、pairing。

abstract.cn: 想象两个零件因被削成相合的形状而咔哒一声接上。

examples.cn: 交配在雨季头几周达到高峰。

examples.en: The two lines were brought together for mating.
examples.cn: 两个品系被放在一起配种。

examples.cn: 密封之前先检查两个面的配合。

root: mate（中低地德语 mate/gemate「同餐伙伴」）+ -ing（古英语 -ung，表动作）；mate 的配偶义自 16 世纪 40 年代，动物配对义自约 1600 年；与 checkmate 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one event: the act of pairing, the season it fills, the system it follows, the strategy it uses, its use in breeding, its technical meaning, the short bond it creates, and finally any matched joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个事件：配对的动作、它占据的季节、它遵循的制度、它采用的策略、它在育种中的用途、它的技术义、它造成的短暂结合，最后是任何相合的结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two creatures or two parts coming together as one matched pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个生物或两个零件合成一对。

branches.en: ACT AND SEASON: the event itself, and the predictable time it fills.
branches.cn: 动作与季节：事件本身，以及它占据的可预测时间。

branches.en: PATTERN AND TACTIC: a species-wide system, and the individual alternatives within it.
branches.cn: 模式与战术：物种层面的制度，以及其中的个体替代方案。

branches.en: CONTROLLED BY PEOPLE: breeders take pairing in hand.
branches.cn: 被人控制：育种者把配对握在手中。

branches.en: PARTS AND BONDS: connectors that must fit, and pairs that last a day.
branches.cn: 零件与结合：必须相合的接头，以及只持续一天的配偶关系。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: anything made to go together.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何被做成相合之物。

intro.en: Mating is a Germanic noun plus the native suffix -ing; there is no Latin element in the word, and its Latin-looking neighbours belong to other families.
intro.cn: mating 是日耳曼语名词加本族后缀 -ing；词中没有拉丁成分，看似拉丁的近邻属于别的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source: mate is Germanic, and the suffix -ing is Old English -ung. Latin has no cognate family here, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁来源：mate 属日耳曼语，后缀 -ing 是古英语 -ung。此处没有拉丁同族词族，故不列拉丁词条。
