definition_zh: 配偶；（动物）配对的对象；伙伴；朋友（英式口语）；交配；配对
definition_en: a partner in a pair, especially for breeding, or to pair with such a partner
core_image: 两只海鸟年复一年在同一块礁石上重逢，替对方理掉颈羽上的盐粒，再合筑一个巢
scene: 两只海鸟年复一年在同一块礁石上重逢，替对方理去颈羽上的盐粒，再合筑一个巢。 Two seabirds meet again on the same rock year after year, preen the salt from each other's neck feathers, and build one nest: each has found a mate for life.
sceneCN: 这里 mate 指「长期共同繁殖的配偶」（第 1 个义项：配偶、配对对象）；句意为两只海鸟年年重逢、互相理羽并合筑一巢，各自找到了终生的配偶。可辨识物件：礁石、相互理羽的两只鸟、同一个巢、海水。

pos.zh: 伙伴；朋友（英式口语，尤用于男性之间）

senses.title: A partner in a breeding pair
senses.definition: one of the two animals or people that form a reproductive pair
senses.definitionCN: 构成繁殖配对的两只动物或两个人之一
senses.example: The male guards the nest while his mate feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 雄性看守巢，配偶外出觅食。
senses.why: The word began as 'one who shares food at the same table', and that image of a shared life became the image of a shared nest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「同桌共食的人」，那幅共享生活的图景后来变成共享巢的图景。

senses.title: A spouse or long-term partner
senses.definition: a husband, wife or long-term romantic partner
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫、妻子或长期恋人
senses.example: He introduced her as his mate, not his girlfriend.
senses.exampleCN: 他介绍她是自己的伴侣，而不是女友。
senses.why: From the 1540s the noun named one of a married pair, and that sense remains the plainest one in many varieties of English.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪 40 年代起，这个名词指已婚一对中的一方，这一义项在许多英语变体中仍是最平实的。

senses.title: A comrade or friend
senses.definition: a friend, especially a male friend addressed informally
senses.definitionCN: 朋友，尤指被随意称呼的男性朋友
senses.example: He turned up with two old mates from the docks.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着两个码头上的老朋友来了。
senses.why: The oldest sense was 'associate, fellow', and it survives in British informal speech long after the breeding sense took over in biology.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「同伴、伙计」，在生物学中繁殖义占主导之后，它仍存活于英式口语中。

senses.title: To pair for breeding
senses.definition: of animals, to come together in order to reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 动物为繁殖而结合在一起
senses.example: The two species rarely mate in the wild.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在野外很少交配。
senses.why: The verb, recorded about 1600 in this sense, simply turned the noun into an action: to become a pair.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在该义项约自 1600 年有记录，只是把名词变成动作：成为一对。

senses.title: To match two things
senses.definition: to join two things that belong together, such as parts or colours
senses.definitionCN: 把两个相配之物接合起来，如零件或颜色
senses.example: The two halves must be mated before the glue sets.
senses.exampleCN: 两半必须在胶凝固之前对接。
senses.why: If a mate is a matching partner, then to mate is to make two things into such a pair, even when neither is alive.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mate 是相配的伙伴，那么 to mate 就是把两物做成这样一对，即便两者都不是活物。

senses.title: A ship's officer
senses.definition: an officer on a merchant ship ranking below the master
senses.definitionCN: 商船上低于船长的驾驶员
senses.example: The mate checked the cargo before departure.
senses.exampleCN: 大副在开船前检查了货物。
senses.why: Shipboard hierarchy borrowed the word for a companion officer, and the rank survives in merchant and fishing fleets.
senses.whyCN: 船上的等级制度借用了这个表示同伴官员的词，这一职衔至今仍存于商船与渔船队。

senses.title: An assistant tradesman
senses.definition: a skilled worker's assistant in a trade, as in plumber's mate
senses.definitionCN: 行业熟练工的助手，如管道工的副手
senses.example: The plumber's mate fetched the right joint.
senses.exampleCN: 管道工的助手取来了合适的接头。
senses.why: In a trade the partner is the one who works alongside, so the word names a role rather than a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 在手艺行当里，伙伴就是并肩干活的人，因此这个词命名一种角色，而非一段关系。

senses.title: Abstract: one of a matched pair
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：相配一对中的一方
senses.definition: one of two things that correspond to each other, such as a glove or a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 彼此对应的两物之一，如手套或鞋
senses.example: He held up the left glove and asked where its mate was.
senses.exampleCN: 他举起左手的手套，问另一只在哪里。
senses.why: At its widest the word needs no animal and no friend: anything that completes a pair can be its mate.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词既不需要动物，也不需要朋友：任何补成一对的东西都能是它的 mate。

intro.en: Mate is a Germanic borrowing, not a Latin word. Middle Low German mate, gemate meant 'one eating at the same table', and English took it in the mid-fourteenth century as 'companion'.
intro.cn: mate 是日耳曼语借词，并非拉丁词。中低地德语 mate、gemate 意为「同桌进食的人」，英语在 14 世纪中叶把它借作「同伴」。

items.en: The compound *ga-matjon meant '(one) having food (*matiz) together (*ga-)'. The same *matiz lies behind English meat.
items.cn: 复合词 *ga-matjon 意为「共同（*ga-）拥有食物（*matiz）的人」。同一个 *matiz 也是英语 meat 的来源。

items.en: Middle Low German mate, gemate 'messmate, companion' is the immediate source, cognate with Dutch maat and German Maat.
items.cn: 中低地德语 mate、gemate「同餐伙伴、同伴」是直接来源，与荷兰语 maat、德语 Maat 同源。

items.en: English mate is recorded from the mid-fourteenth century meaning 'associate, fellow', and as a form of address among sailors and workers.
items.cn: 英语 mate 自 14 世纪中叶有记录，义为「伙伴、伙计」，并在水手与工人间用作称呼。

items.en: The sense 'one of a married pair' is recorded from the 1540s; the verb 'to pair, couple' from about 1500, with the animal sense from about 1600.
items.cn: 「已婚一对中的一方」义自 16 世纪 40 年代有记录；动词「配对、结合」约自 1500 年，动物交配义约自 1600 年。

items.en: The mate of checkmate is a different word: it comes through Old French from Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless'.
items.cn: checkmate 中的 mate 是另一个词：经古法语来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the reconstruction of *matiz and its wider Indo-European links is debated, and the exact first date of the nautical rank is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*matiz 的重构及其更广的印欧语联系存有争论；航海职衔的确切首见年代也无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the verb forms, the informal adjective and the unrelated chess word; group two holds nouns for a partner under different descriptions.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词形式、口语形容词与无关的国际象棋词；第二组是以不同描述指伴侣的名词。

entries.definition: The gerund of the verb: the act or period of pairing.
entries.definitionCN: 该动词的动名词：配对的动作或时期。

entries.definition: British informal 'friendly', built on the companion sense; it has no biological meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「友好的」，建立在同伴义上；无生物学含义。

entries.definition: A fellow member of a class; the second element still means companion, not breeding partner.
entries.definitionCN: 同班成员；第二个成分仍是「同伴」，而非繁殖配偶。

entries.definition: From Persian shah mat 'the king is helpless': a chess term with no connection to companion or spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 来自波斯语 shah mat「王已无路可走」：国际象棋术语，与同伴或配偶无关。

entries.definition: A person one shares an activity, business or life with; wider than mate and often less biological.
entries.definitionCN: 共同从事活动、事业或生活的人；比 mate 更宽，常少些生物学色彩。

entries.definition: A husband or wife in a legal marriage; mate can be used far more loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 合法婚姻中的丈夫或妻子；mate 的用法远为宽松。

entries.definition: Someone who accompanies another; from Latin panis 'bread', the very image behind mate.
entries.definitionCN: 陪伴他人的人；来自拉丁 panis「面包」，正是 mate 背后的图景。

entries.definition: A person or thing holding the same role elsewhere; it stresses correspondence, not companionship.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处担任同样角色的人或物；强调对应，而非陪伴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.cn: mate 来自「同桌的人」，所以配偶字面上就是共享餐桌的人。

normal.en: The family runs mate, mating, mated, matey, classmate, roommate, soulmate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mate、mating、mated、matey、classmate、roommate、soulmate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mate for life, find a mate, choose a mate, mate with.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：终生配对、寻找配偶、选择配偶、与……交配。

normal.en: Checkmate looks like a relative but comes from Persian.
normal.cn: checkmate 看似同族，其实来自波斯语。

normal.en: The nautical rank survives in merchant ships: the chief mate is below the master.
normal.cn: 航海职衔仍存于商船：大副在船长之下。

abstract.en: Picture two birds sharing one rock as if it were one table.
abstract.cn: 想象两只鸟共用一个礁石，仿佛那是同一张餐桌。

abstract.en: Picture a left glove waiting in a drawer for its other half.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里一只左手手套等着另一半。

abstract.en: Picture two parts that were machined to meet and cannot mistake each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个被加工成彼此相合、不会认错的零件。

examples.en: The pair stays together for several seasons, mating on the same ledge.
examples.cn: 这一对会相伴数季，在同一处岩架上交配。

examples.en: He came to the party with an old mate from school.
examples.cn: 他带着一位老同学来参加聚会。

examples.cn: 她找不到那只耳环的另一只。

root: 中低地德语 mate/gemate「同桌共食者」← 原始日耳曼 *ga-matjon（*ga- 共同 + *matiz 食物）；与拉丁语无关，与 checkmate（波斯语 shah mat）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one word from a table companion to a breeding partner, a spouse, a friend, an act of pairing, a mechanical fit, a ship's officer, an assistant, and finally either half of any pair.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个词：从同桌的伙伴，到繁殖配偶、配偶、朋友、配对动作、机械配合、船上大副、行业助手，最后是任何一对中的任一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lives sharing one place, one table or one nest.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条生命共用一处地方、一张桌子或一个巢。

branches.en: SHARED LIFE: the biological partner, then the married one.
branches.cn: 共享生活：先是生物学配偶，再是婚姻配偶。

branches.en: SHARED WORK: the comrade at large, and the assistant in a trade.
branches.cn: 共享工作：广义的伙伴，以及行当中的助手。

branches.en: BECOMING A PAIR: animals pair, and parts are made to fit.
branches.cn: 成为一对：动物配对，零件被做成相合。

branches.en: A ROLE ON SHIP: the companion officer of the master.
branches.cn: 船上的角色：船长的同伴官员。

branches.en: WIDEST SCOPE: anything that completes a pair.
branches.cn: 最宽的范围：任何补成一对的东西。

intro.en: Mate is a Germanic noun and verb with no Latin element; its compounds are all native formations, which makes the word a good test of etymological honesty.
intro.cn: mate 是日耳曼语名词与动词，不含拉丁成分；其复合词都是本族构成，因此这个词很适合检验词源诚实度。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries: mate is Germanic, and the apparent Latin neighbours (as in checkmate) come from Persian. Latin supplied nothing here.
latinIntro.cn: 不列拉丁词条：mate 属日耳曼语，看似拉丁的近邻（如 checkmate）来自波斯语。拉丁语在此没有贡献。

definition_zh: 交配行为：动物在配对与繁殖过程中表现出的成套行为
definition_en: the set of actions an animal performs in order to obtain a partner and reproduce
core_image: 雄性先把石子排成一条整齐的线，再绕石子转圈，雌性只在石线完整时才靠近
scene: 雄性先把小石子排成一条线，再绕石子转圈，雌性只在石线完整时才靠近。 The male arranges pebbles in a line and circles them, and the female approaches only when the line is complete, a mating behavior that depends on the display rather than on the male himself.
sceneCN: 这里 mating behavior 指「为获得配偶与繁殖而表现出的成套行为」（第 1 个义项：交配行为总称）；句意为雄性排石转圈、雌性在石线完整时才靠近，这一交配行为取决于展示本身而非雄性个体。可辨识物件：排成线的石子、转圈的雄性、观察的雌性、水边。

pos.zh: 某种特定的交配行为模式（可数，a mating behavior）

forms.label: 复数（多种交配行为模式）

senses.title: The whole set of reproductive actions
senses.definition: all the actions an animal performs in connection with finding a partner and reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 动物在寻找配偶与繁殖方面所做全部动作的总和
senses.example: The chapter surveys mating behavior across mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章综述哺乳动物的交配行为。
senses.why: The compound joins an event to its conduct, so it can name the whole repertoire rather than one act.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把一个事件与它的举止连在一起，因此能命名整套动作，而非单个行为。

senses.title: The courtship-to-copulation sequence
senses.definition: the ordered sequence that begins with courtship and ends with copulation
senses.definitionCN: 以求偶开始、以交配结束的按序过程
senses.example: The mating behavior begins with a call and ends with the pair leaving together.
senses.exampleCN: 这一交配行为以鸣叫开始，以成对离开结束。
senses.why: Because reproduction is a process, the compound can name the sequence as a whole, with its own order and timing.
senses.whyCN: 因为繁殖是一个过程，这个复合词能命名整个序列，包含它自身的次序与时机。

senses.title: A mating strategy or tactic
senses.definition: one of the alternative tactics used to obtain mates, such as guarding or sneaking
senses.definitionCN: 为获得配偶而采用的替代战术之一，如守卫或偷袭
senses.example: Sneaking is a mating behavior that avoids direct competition.
senses.exampleCN: 偷袭是一种避开直接竞争的交配行为。
senses.why: Once pairing is a problem with alternatives, each alternative can be called a behavior and compared with the others.
senses.whyCN: 一旦配对成为有替代方案的问题，每个方案都能被称为一种行为，并与其他方案比较。

senses.title: A species' mating system in action
senses.titleCN: 物种交配制度的实际表现
senses.definition: the observable conduct through which a species' mating system is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种的交配制度借以表现的可观察举止
senses.example: The mating behavior matches the species' monogamous system.
senses.exampleCN: 其交配行为与该物种的一雄一雌制度相符。
senses.why: A system is an abstraction until it is performed, and the compound names the performance.
senses.whyCN: 制度在被执行之前只是抽象物，而这个复合词命名执行本身。

senses.title: A fixed action pattern before mating
senses.titleCN: 交配前的固定动作模式
senses.definition: a stereotyped, repeatable movement that must occur before a partner will accept mating
senses.definitionCN: 配偶接受交配之前必须出现的刻板、可重复动作
senses.example: The bow is a mating behavior that cannot be omitted.
senses.exampleCN: 鞠躬是一种不可省略的交配行为。
senses.why: Where acceptance depends on a signal, the signal becomes a required unit, and the compound names such units collectively.
senses.whyCN: 当接受取决于某个信号，该信号就成为必需单位，这个复合词便总称这类单位。

senses.title: The object of sexual-selection study
senses.definition: the conduct that sexual selection acts on, especially choice and competition
senses.definitionCN: 性选择所作用的举止，尤其是选择与竞争
senses.example: Sexual selection explains why the mating behavior is so elaborate.
senses.exampleCN: 性选择解释了这套交配行为为何如此繁复。
senses.why: If mating success differs among individuals, then the conduct that wins or loses mates is exactly what selection can act on.
senses.whyCN: 如果交配成功率在个体间不同，那么决定胜负的举止正是选择可以作用的东西。

senses.title: Mating behavior in captivity
senses.titleCN: 圈养条件下的交配行为
senses.definition: the reproductive conduct of animals kept by humans, often altered by confinement
senses.definitionCN: 被人饲养的动物的繁殖举止，常因圈养而改变
senses.example: The zoo recorded mating behavior that never appears in the wild.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园记录到野外从未出现的交配行为。
senses.why: Confinement changes conditions, and changed conditions change conduct, so the compound is used to compare captive with wild.
senses.whyCN: 圈养改变条件，条件改变举止，因此这个复合词被用来比较圈养与野生。

senses.title: Abstract: the programme before a union
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：结合之前的一整套程序
senses.definition: any set of steps by which two parties are brought into a union
senses.definitionCN: 把双方带入结合的任何成套步骤
senses.example: The firm's mating behavior with partners is slow and cautious.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司与伙伴结合的程序缓慢而谨慎。
senses.why: At its widest, the compound becomes a template for any merger, biological or corporate.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个复合词成了任何合并的模板，无论生物的还是企业的。

intro.en: Mating behavior is a twentieth-century compound of mating (from mate) and behavior (from behave). Both halves are Germanic, so the phrase has no Latin ancestry.
intro.cn: mating behavior 是 20 世纪的复合词，由 mating（源自 mate）与 behavior（源自 behave）构成。两部分都属日耳曼语，因此这个短语没有拉丁来源。

items.en: Mate came from Middle Low German mate 'table companion'; the verb 'to pair for breeding' dates from about 1600, and mating is its gerund.
items.cn: mate 来自中低地德语 mate「同桌伙伴」；动词「为繁殖而配对」约自 1600 年，mating 是其动名词。

items.en: Behavior came from behave, literally 'to carry oneself', and is recorded from the late fifteenth century.
items.cn: behavior 来自 behave，字面为「把握自己」，自 15 世纪晚期有记录。

items.en: The phrase mating behavior belongs to twentieth-century ethology and psychology, where observable conduct was being catalogued and compared.
items.cn: mating behavior 这一短语属于 20 世纪的行为学与心理学，当时可观察的举止正被编目与比较。

items.en: As the study of animal behavior expanded, the phrase appeared in textbooks and became a standard heading in zoology.
items.cn: 随着动物行为研究扩展，这个短语进入教科书，成为动物学的标准标题。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single earliest citation for the exact phrase is agreed, so the twentieth-century date should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个确切短语的最早书证没有统一说法，因此 20 世纪这一年代应视为约数。

items.en: The mate of mating is the companion word, not the chess mate of checkmate, which came from Persian shah mat.
items.cn: mating 中的 mate 是「同伴」那个词，而非 checkmate 中的国际象棋 mate；后者来自波斯语 shah mat。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves of the compound and its spelling variants; group two holds related terms for different parts of the reproductive sequence.
note.cn: 第一组区分复合词的两半及其拼写变体；第二组是繁殖序列不同部分的相关术语。

entries.definition: The pairing event alone; the compound adds the conduct that surrounds it.
entries.definitionCN: 只指配对事件；复合词加上围绕它的一整套举止。

entries.definition: Conduct in general; only when joined to mating does it name reproductive conduct specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指的举止；只有与 mating 结合，才专指繁殖举止。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of behavior', used in behavioral ecology and behavioral studies.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「行为的」的形容词，用于行为生态学与行为研究。

entries.definition: The social pattern of pairing, such as monogamy; it is the rule, while mating behavior is the performance.
entries.definitionCN: 配对的社会模式，如一雄一雌；它是规则，而 mating behavior 是执行。

entries.definition: The displays that precede mating and often decide whether it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 交配之前的展示，常决定交配是否发生。

entries.definition: The physical act of union; mating behavior is the wider set that includes it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体结合的动作；mating behavior 是包含它的更广集合。

entries.definition: The forming of pairs, which may occur without reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形成一对，可能不涉及繁殖。

entries.definition: The whole reproductive process, including care of eggs and young.
entries.definitionCN: 整个繁殖过程，包括照顾卵与幼体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mating + behavior: the conduct that surrounds pairing.
normal.cn: mating + behavior：围绕配对的一整套举止。

normal.en: The family runs mate, mating, behavior, behavioral, mating system.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mate、mating、behavior、behavioral、交配制度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: study mating behavior, seasonal mating behavior, mating behavior in birds.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：研究交配行为、季节性交配行为、鸟类的交配行为。

normal.en: British spelling: mating behaviour.
normal.cn: 英式拼写：mating behaviour。

normal.en: The phrase belongs to ethology: it names what can be seen, not what is felt.
normal.cn: 这个短语属于行为学：命名可见之物，而非感受。

abstract.en: Picture a line of pebbles that must be complete before anyone approaches.
abstract.cn: 想象一条必须先排完整的石子线，才有人靠近。

abstract.en: Picture a dance whose steps are a contract.
abstract.cn: 想象一支舞，舞步本身就是契约。

abstract.en: Picture two companies circling each other as carefully as two birds.
abstract.cn: 想象两家公司像两只鸟一样谨慎地绕圈。

examples.en: The textbook devotes a chapter to mating behavior in insects.
examples.cn: 这本教科书用一章讲昆虫的交配行为。

examples.en: Confinement changed the animals' mating behavior within one generation.
examples.cn: 圈养在一代之内就改变了这些动物的交配行为。

examples.en: Sexual selection explains the extremes of mating behavior.
examples.cn: 性选择解释了交配行为的极端表现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mating（交配）+ behavior（行为）」——围绕配对发生的一整套动作 → 交配行为

root: mating（mate 的动名词，mate 来自中低地德语「同桌伙伴」）+ behavior（behave：be- + have）；两部分均属日耳曼语，无拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole repertoire, through sequence, tactic, system, fixed unit, object of selection, captive case, and finally any programme before a union.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整套动作出发，经序列、战术、制度、固定单位、选择对象、圈养情形，最后到任何结合前的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a set of steps that must be performed before two animals become a pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只动物成为一对之前必须完成的一套步骤。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND ITS ORDER: a repertoire, then the sequence it follows.
branches.cn: 整体与次序：一整套动作，以及它遵循的序列。

branches.en: STRATEGY AND RULE: individual tactics, and the species system they enact.
branches.cn: 战术与规则：个体战术，以及它们执行的物种制度。

branches.en: UNITS UNDER SELECTION: required movements, and the conduct selection acts on.
branches.cn: 受选择的单位：必需动作，以及选择所作用的举止。

branches.en: CHANGED CONDITIONS: captivity rewrites the repertoire.
branches.cn: 改变的条件：圈养重写整套动作。

branches.en: WIDEST TEMPLATE: any steps before a merger.
branches.cn: 最宽的模板：任何合并之前的步骤。

intro.en: Mating behavior is a two-word compound of native Germanic material; neither half has a Latin root, which is unusual in this academic vocabulary.
intro.cn: mating behavior 是由本族日耳曼语材料构成的两词复合词；两半都没有拉丁词根，这在这类学术词汇中并不常见。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries: mate and behavior are both Germanic, and the suffix -ing is Old English -ung. Nothing here comes from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 不列拉丁词条：mate 与 behavior 都属日耳曼语，后缀 -ing 是古英语 -ung。此处没有任何成分来自拉丁语。

items.example: Mating precedes the behavior studied here.
items.exampleCN: 交配先于这里所研究的行为。

items.example: Behavior is what can be observed.
items.exampleCN: 行为就是可被观察之物。

items.example: The study filmed mating behavior for a year.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究拍了一年的交配行为。

items.example: The book lists mating behaviours by family.
items.exampleCN: 这本书按科列出交配行为。

items.example: Behavioral studies code the same acts.
items.exampleCN: 行为研究给同样的动作编码。

items.example: The mating system predicts the behavior.
items.exampleCN: 交配制度预测这一行为。

items.example: Courtship is the first part of mating behavior.
items.exampleCN: 求偶是交配行为的第一部分。

items.example: A mate is found before mating begins.
items.exampleCN: 交配开始前先找到配偶。

items.example: The mated pair stayed on the same ledge.
items.exampleCN: 已配对的一对留在同一岩架。

definition_zh: 攻击行为；侵略；挑衅；攻击性；侵袭性
definition_en: hostile behaviour aimed at harming or dominating another, or an unprovoked act of attack
core_image: 一只狗把身体压低在门口，龇牙低吼，把来客挡在门槛之外
scene: 两只陌生的公羊在狭窄的山道上迎面相遇，一只先后退半步，随即低头冲撞过去，另一只也不肯让路。 Two unfamiliar rams meet head-on along a narrow trail, and one steps back only to charge with lowered horns, an act of aggression that decides which of them passes first.
sceneCN: 这里 aggression 指「以伤害或压制对方为目的的敌对行为」（第 1 个义项：对另一方的直接攻击）；句意为两只陌生公羊在山道上相遇，一只后退后立即低头冲撞，用攻击决定谁先通过。可辨识物件：狭窄山道、低垂的羊角、后退再前冲的姿势、不肯退让的另一只羊。

forms.label: 形容词（侵略的；有攻击性的）

derivatives.zh: 侵略的；有攻击性的；积极进取的
发动侵略；挑起攻击（罕用）

senses.title: Direct hostile behaviour
senses.definition: behaviour intended to hurt, intimidate or drive off another individual
senses.definitionCN: 意在伤害、威吓或赶走另一个体的行为
senses.example: The rams' aggression settled the dispute over the narrow trail.
senses.exampleCN: 公羊的攻击行为解决了山道通行权的争端。
senses.why: Aggression names the act of stepping toward someone with intent to harm, so the plainest sense is the visible hostile move itself.
senses.whyCN: aggression 本指「朝某人迈步而去、意在加害」的动作，因此最平实的义项就是看得见的敌意举动。

senses.title: An unprovoked attack by a state
senses.definition: an attack by one country on another without just cause
senses.definitionCN: 一国无正当理由对另一国发动的攻击
senses.example: The treaty defined aggression as any armed crossing of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把侵略界定为任何武装越界行为。
senses.why: One individual stepping toward another became one state moving its army across a frontier, and international law fixed that enlarged sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个人朝另一个人迈步，扩展为一国把军队开过边界；国际法把这一放大的义项固定下来。

senses.title: Hostile words or manner
senses.definition: spoken or written hostility that threatens or belittles another person
senses.definitionCN: 威胁或贬低他人的口头或书面敌意
senses.example: Her aggression in the meeting silenced the junior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上的咄咄逼人让年轻员工不敢作声。
senses.why: If a step toward someone can wound, then words that step toward someone can wound too, so the noun spread from blows to tone.
senses.whyCN: 如果朝人迈出的一步能伤人，那么朝人而来的话语也能伤人，于是这个词从拳脚扩展到语气。

senses.title: An inner drive in psychology
senses.definition: an internal impulse or tendency that pushes a person or animal toward hostile action
senses.definitionCN: 推动人或动物作出敌对行动的内在冲动或倾向
senses.example: The experiment measured aggression as a score, not as a blow.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验把攻击性量化为分数，而不是实际打击。
senses.why: Psychology turned the outward act into an inward quantity, so aggression came to name the force behind the behaviour rather than the behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把向外发生的动作转为内在的量，于是 aggression 开始指行为背后的力，而非行为本身。

senses.title: Invasive growth in medicine
senses.definition: the tendency of a disease or tumour to spread into surrounding tissue
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或肿瘤向周围组织扩散的趋势
senses.example: The pathologist graded the tumour by its aggression.
senses.exampleCN: 病理学家按侵袭性给肿瘤分级。
senses.why: A tumour that pushes into healthy tissue repeats the old image of something advancing where it is not wanted, so medicine reused the word.
senses.whyCN: 肿瘤挤入健康组织，重现了「不该来的东西向前推进」这一古老意象，医学便再次启用这个词。

senses.title: Economic or commercial expansion
senses.titleCN: 经济或商业上的扩张侵略
senses.definition: forceful expansion by a company or economy into another's market
senses.definitionCN: 公司或经济力量强行进入他方市场
senses.example: Critics called the takeover corporate aggression.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这次收购称为企业侵略。
senses.why: The frontier moved again, this time from a border to a market share, and the metaphor kept its disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 边界再次移动，这一次从国界移到市场份额，这个比喻保留了它的贬义。

senses.title: Forceful assertiveness
senses.definition: vigorous, forceful energy in pursuing a goal, viewed without moral blame
senses.definitionCN: 追求目标时强劲有力的劲头，不带道德指责
senses.example: Sales staff were praised for their aggression in a tight market.
senses.exampleCN: 销售人员在紧俏市场中的拼劲受到称赞。
senses.why: Once the hostile edge is removed, the same forward push can be read as drive, and business writing often uses it that way.
senses.whyCN: 一旦去掉敌意，同样的向前推进便可读作干劲，商业写作常这样使用。

senses.title: Abstract: encroachment on any boundary
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对任何边界的侵越
senses.definition: any unwanted advance into another's space, rights or domain
senses.definitionCN: 对他人空间、权利或领域的任何不受欢迎的推进
senses.example: Noise from the new road was felt as aggression against the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 新公路的噪音被当作对山谷的侵扰。
senses.why: At its widest the word needs no army and no animal: anything that presses into a space it was not invited to can be called aggression.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽泛的用法里，这个词既不需要军队也不需要动物：任何挤入未受邀之地的力量都可称为 aggression。

intro.en: Aggression comes from Latin aggressio 'an attack', from aggredi 'to go toward, attack', built on ad- 'toward' and gradi 'to step, walk'. English took it in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aggression 来自拉丁 aggressio「攻击」，源自动词 aggredi「走向、攻击」，由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「迈步、行走」构成。英语在 17 世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gradi meant 'to step, walk, go'. It also gives gradus 'step', the source of grade and gradual. Its deeper Indo-European origin is usually reconstructed as a root meaning 'to walk', but that form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走」。它也给出 gradus「步」，是 grade 与 gradual 的来源。其更早的印欧语来源通常被重构为表「行走」的词根，但那是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus gradi produced aggredi, literally 'to step toward', and in use 'to set upon, attack'. The literal and the hostile readings coexisted from the start.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，字面为「朝……迈步」，实际使用中义为「扑向、攻击」。字面义与敌意义从一开始就并存。

items.en: The noun aggressio 'an attack, an assault' was formed on the participle stem aggress-, so the word carries the image of a step already taken.
items.cn: 名词 aggressio「攻击、进犯」由分词词干 aggress- 构成，因此这个词带着「已经迈出的一步」的意象。

items.en: English aggression is recorded from the seventeenth century in the sense of an unprovoked attack; earlier uses were rare and mostly literal.
items.cn: 英语 aggression 自 17 世纪有记录，义为「无端攻击」；更早的用法罕见，且多为字面义。

items.en: In the twentieth century international law fixed aggression as a legal category, and psychology extended it to an inner drive measurable in tests.
items.cn: 20 世纪，国际法把 aggression 固定为法律范畴，心理学则把它扩展为可在测验中测量的内在驱力。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): dictionaries do not agree on the exact earliest citation for the hostile sense or for the psychological sense, and the reconstruction of the pre-Latin root of gradi remains a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代：更深词根亦属重构）：各词典对敌意义与心理学义的最早书证并不一致；gradi 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，并非有文献可查的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin step-root that are easy to confuse; group two holds near synonyms that differ in who acts and how openly.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「迈步」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是近义词，区别在于谁在行动、行动有多公开。

entries.definition: The adjective from the same stem: ready to attack, or merely forceful in pursuit of a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干的形容词：随时准备攻击，或仅在追求目标时强劲有力。

entries.definition: The one who begins the attack; the noun names the agent, while aggression names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 首先发动攻击的一方；该名词指行动者，而 aggression 指行为本身。

entries.definition: Built on ex- 'out' plus gradi: a going out, the mirror image of a step toward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「向外」加 gradi 构成：走出去，正好是「朝……迈步」的反向镜像。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus gradi: to step backward, hence to return to an earlier state; it shares the root but not the hostility.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 gradi：向后迈步，因而指退回较早状态；同词根，但不含敌意。

entries.definition: One concrete act of striking; aggression can also be a standing tendency or a national policy.
entries.definitionCN: 一次具体的打击行动；aggression 也可指长期倾向或国家政策。

entries.definition: An unfriendly attitude that may never become a blow; aggression implies that the hostility is acted out.
entries.definitionCN: 未必化为行动的敌意态度；aggression 则意味敌意已被付诸行动。

entries.definition: A violent physical or legal attack on a person; narrower and more concrete than aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 对人身实施的暴力或法律意义上的侵犯；比 aggression 更窄、更具体。

entries.definition: An entry by force into another's territory; it stresses crossing a border, while aggression stresses the hostile intent.
entries.definitionCN: 武力进入他方领土；强调越过边界，而 aggression 强调敌意本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' plus gradi 'to step': aggression is a step taken toward someone with intent to do harm.
normal.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi「迈步」：aggression 就是带着加害意图朝某人迈出的一步。

normal.en: The family runs aggress, aggression, aggressive, aggressively, aggressiveness, aggressor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aggress、aggression、aggressive、aggressively、aggressiveness、aggressor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: military aggression, acts of aggression, aggression against, verbal aggression.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：军事侵略、侵略行为、对……的侵略、言语攻击。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with egress or regress: those are steps out and steps back, not steps toward.
normal.cn: 不要与 egress 或 regress 混淆：那两个是向外走与向后退，而不是朝前迈。

normal.en: In medicine the same word describes a tumour that steps into healthy tissue.
normal.cn: 在医学中，同一个词描述肿瘤「迈入」健康组织。

abstract.en: Picture a boot stepping over a line drawn in the dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子跨过画在尘土上的界线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a door that was never opened for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去推一扇从未为它打开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a tide that keeps rising into a garden nobody meant to flood.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水不断上涨，淹进一座本不该被淹的花园。

examples.en: The study links early aggression in children to later conflict at school.
examples.cn: 这项研究把儿童早期的攻击行为与日后的校园冲突联系起来。

examples.en: The council condemned the aggression as a breach of the treaty.
examples.cn: 理事会谴责这次侵略违反了条约。

examples.en: Biologists recorded every act of aggression at the feeding site.
examples.cn: 生物学家记录了觅食点上每一次攻击行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a（一个）+ gress（迈步）+ ion」——朝你迈出的一步 → 攻击、侵略

root: 拉丁 aggressio「攻击」← aggredi「走向、扑向」= ad-「朝向」+ gradi「迈步」；gradi 更深词根为重构形式；与 egress（向外走）、regress（向后退）同词根而方向不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a single hostile act, through war, words, inner drive, disease, markets, and plain drive, to any unwanted advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一次敌对举动出发，经战争、言语、内在驱力、疾病、市场与单纯的干劲，最后到任何不受欢迎的推进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken toward another with the intent to harm or push past a limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：带着加害或越界的意图，朝另一方迈出的一步。

branches.en: DIRECT AND SPOKEN: a physical hostile move, and the same move made in words.
branches.cn: 直接与言语：身体上的敌意举动，以及用言语完成的同一举动。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE ADVANCE: a state crossing a border, and a company crossing into a market.
branches.cn: 集体推进：国家越过国界，公司越入市场。

branches.en: INSIDE THE ACTOR: the impulse measured instead of the blow struck.
branches.cn: 行动者内部：被测量的冲动，而非已落下的打击。

branches.en: INTO THE BODY: a growth that steps into healthy tissue.
branches.cn: 进入身体：迈入健康组织的生长。

branches.en: WITHOUT BLAME: forceful drive praised, and any encroachment named.
branches.cn: 去掉指责：受称赞的强劲干劲，以及任何被指名的侵越。

intro.en: Aggression is built from two Latin pieces that also form many everyday English words, so the spelling can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: aggression 由两个拉丁成分构成，这两个成分也构成许多日常英语词，因此这个词的拼写可以按语素来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin aggredi and its noun aggressio give the English word; the prefix ad- and the root gradi recur in other words, though not every look-alike shares the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aggredi 及其名词 aggressio 给出这个英语词；前缀 ad- 与词根 gradi 在别的词中重现，但并非所有形近词都共用这个词根。

items.example: The prefix turns a bare step into a step aimed at someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把单纯的迈步变成朝某人迈出的步。

items.example: The root supplies the walking image behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供整个词族背后的行走意象。

items.example: The stem appears in progress, regress and egress.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 progress、regress 与 egress 中。

items.example: The stem carries both the literal and the hostile reading.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干同时承载字面义与敌意义。

items.example: It turns the act of attacking into the name of the act.
items.exampleCN: 它把攻击的动作变成这一动作的名称。

items.example: Aggressive is the adjective of tendency built on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: aggressive 是同词干上表倾向的形容词。

items.example: Aggressor names the one who takes the first step.
items.exampleCN: aggressor 指先迈出那一步的人。

items.example: Aggressiveness names the quality measured in tests.
items.exampleCN: aggressiveness 指测验中测量的那种性质。
